Sports.title: Arsenal in talks over Jarell Quansah deal as England star lined up for unexpected Premier League return
Sports.content:
Arsenal in talks over Jarell Quansah deal as England star lined up for unexpected Premier League return

Arsenal are in discussions with Bayer Leverkusen over a deal for Jarell Quansah, talkSPORT understands.

Quansah has been with the German club for just one season following his £35million move from Liverpool last summer.

2 Could Quansah return to the Premier League in a red kit that isn't Liverpool's? Credit: Getty

Despite the Gunners' interest, it may prove a difficult deal to get done.

What is Bayer Leverkusen's stance on Jarrel Quansah?

It is understood Leverkusen do not want to sell the England international.

And even if they did, the club would want to make a profit on the eight-figure sum they paid to sign him from Liverpool.

The Reds did have the option to re-sign Quansah this summer for £70m, but they elected not to trigger it.

Had they done so, Quansah, who came through Liverpool's academy, would have become the club's second-most expensive defensive signing.

Arsenal's mooted pursuit of Quansah comes on the eve of their season getting underway.

The Gunners face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday, live on talkSPORT.

Mikel Arteta's side then begin their Premier League title defence on August 21 against Coventry City, which is also live on talkSPORT.

Which other defenders have Arsenal targeted this window?

Arsenal have already shown a willingness to improve their defensive stocks by going after Aston Villa centre-back Ezri Konsa.

The Gunners have already made a verbal offer to Villa for Konsa in the region of £35m.

2 Konsa has been with Villa since 2019 and still has two years to run on his contract Credit: Getty

However, this fell well below Villa's valuation of Konsa, who are looking for as much as £65m.

Arsenal had also been linked with a sensational swoop for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

However, Romero is instead set to join Atletico Madrid in a deal worth approximately £34m.

The Gunners are on the lookout for defensive reinforcements with starting defender William Saliba set to miss an 'extended period' with a back issue he picked up at the World Cup.

Adding to Arsenal's woes at the back is Jurrien Timber, who continues to recover from a groin injury.

The duo's fitness issues leaves Gabriel, Piero Hincapie and Cristhian Mosquera as the primary centre-back options.

Left-back Riccardo Calafiori is capable of playing at centre-back as well.

Sports.title: Legendary goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer dies aged 78 as Aston Villa pay tribute
Sports.content:
Legendary Aston Villa goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has passed away.

Rimmer, who also played for Manchester United and Arsenal, was 78 at the time of his passing.

2 Rimmer made just shy of 290 appearances for Villa Credit: Getty

Aston Villa release statement on Jimmy Rimmer's passing

"Rimmer was one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation, and arguably one of the unluckiest when it came to big occasions," a Villa statement read.

"Despite collecting two European Cup winner’s medals, he wasn’t on the pitch at the end of either final.

"He was on the bench at Wembley in 1968 as Manchester United beat Benfica 4-1 and played for just nine minutes for Villa against Bayern Munich in 1982 before a neck injury forced him to be substituted by Nigel Spink in Rotterdam.

"Rimmer was in tears in the dressing room as he received treatment from club doctor David Targett, although he was back in the dug-out in time to witness Peter Withe’s winning goal and join in the post-match celebrations.

"Even so, he was one of just five Villa players to figure in the starting line-up in all nine of our European Cup matches that season – and had been one of seven ever-presents in the title-winning campaign of 1980-81."

Jimmy Rimmer's career at a glance

Rimmer joined United as a schoolboy in 1963 and turned professional only two years later.

The gloveman remained at Old Trafford for 11 years, although it was primarily spent as Alex Stepney's understudy.

Rimmer then joined Arsenal in 1974.

During his time with the Gunners, Rimmer won his first and only England cap.

Rimmer moved to Aston Villa after three years in north London for just £65,000.

2 Rimmer (centre) was one of Villa's heroes in 1982, even if his game time was brutally cut short Credit: Getty

He went on to make 287 appearances for the West Midlands club across all competitions.

Rimmer called time on his Villa career in 1983 when he joined Swansea.

The Southport native hung up the gloves in 1986 and later moved into coaching.

Rimmer even had two brief spells as caretaker boss of Swansea during the 1995/96 season.

After the tragic news of Rimmer's passing was confirmed, his former United teammate Stepney wrote on X: "Such sad news to hear Jimmy Rimmer has passed away, rest in peace and lots of love to Jimmy's family."

Wayne Barton, who has penned a number of United-related books, said: "Rest in peace Jimmy Rimmer. Incredibly nice guy. A unique place in football history is his."

Sports.title: Burnley terminate deal and announce new one in kit chaos days before season opener
Sports.content:
Burnley terminate deal and announce new one in kit chaos days before season opener

Burnley were given an unwanted headache on the eve of the new Championship season.

The Clarets' new front-of-shirt sponsor, Finotive One, will no longer adorn their kit.

3 Finotive One had a short spell as Burnley's front-of-shirt sponsor Credit: Getty

Instead, they will be sponsored by Vertu, with the announcement made days before their Championship season opener against West Ham on Sunday, which is live on talkSPORT 2.

Burnley issue statement on Finotive One

"Burnley Football Club is disappointed to confirm that its agreement with Finotive has been terminated," a Burnley club statement read.

"We have acted decisively to protect the Club’s interests, and those of our supporters, while ensuring preparations for the new season continue uninterrupted, both on and off the pitch."

The club has confirmed fans who already purchased a new kit with Finotive One's branding can either claim a full refund, exchange their shirt for a replacement featuring Vertu branding or have Vertu branding applied to their existing kit free of charge.

Burnley initially announced the partnership with Finotive One in early July, with the Cypriot-registered company to feature on their playing and training kits.

The arrangement was in place for the entirety of the 2026/27 season and the Clarets had even played a competitive match in a kit which featured Finotive One's branding.

However, that partnership was plunged into uncertainty when Sky Sports wiped the sponsor from the Clarets' kit in graphics promoting the club's Championship season opener.

Adding to the chaos was that Burnley appeared to have taken down the article on the club website where they announced Finotive One as the new sponsor.

Vertu officially takes over as Burnley's new front-of-shirt sponsor

Finotive One was also listed among Burnley's partner and sponsor section on the website until 9am on Friday, when they were officially replaced by Vertu.

“We are delighted to welcome Vertu as Burnley Football Club’s new Official Front of Shirt Principal Partner," Burnley chairman Alan Pace said.

3 Clarets boss Nicky Hayen will hope the sponsorship circus won't derail his side on Sunday Credit: Getty

"Vertu has been a valued and trusted partner of the Club, and this new relationship is a natural next step for two organisations that share a commitment to ambition, innovation and long-term success.

“From our very first conversations, it was clear there was a shared vision for what this new partnership could achieve, and we look forward to working even more closely together and creating exciting new opportunities for our supporters throughout the season.”

Finotive One, a Cypriot-registered company, replaced betting firm 96.com as Burnley's front-of-shirt sponsor due to the ban on gambling sponsors coming into effect.

In a statement announcing the partnership, Burnley described Finotive One as a 'global trading ecosystem' which supported 'tens of thousands of traders worldwide through its integrated platforms spanning funding, trading infrastructure, payments, and market access.'

Burnley will look to shake off the sponsorship drama on Sunday against the Hammers as both sides look to secure an instant return to the Premier League.

The Clarets finished 19th with 22 points while West Ham were relegated on the final day last term.

3 Burnley suffered relegation for the third time in five seasons last term Credit: Getty

In a bid to immediately bounce back, Burnley appointed Nicky Hayen as their new manager.

Hayen was handed the reins after ex-Wolves boss Rob Edwards rejected an approach.

Wales boss Craig Bellamy had also been a serious contender for the post, only for Burnley to pull out of talks.

Sports.title: Burnley vs West Ham LIVE commentary: Hammers begin first Championship seasons in 14 years
Sports.content:
Burnley vs West Ham LIVE commentary: Hammers begin first Championship seasons in 14 years

Burnley and West Ham have been handed a difficult test for their Championship returns this weekend.

The two sides will meet each other at Turf Moor following their relegations from the Premier League last season.



3 Nuno Espirito Santo is ready to kickstart West Ham's quest for promotion Credit: Getty

For the home side it marked their third relegation in five campaigns, whilst their last two at this level have both ended in promotion.

As for the Hammers, they failed to secure Premier League survival on the final day of the season.

Nuno Espitio Santo's side will now play in the Championship for the first time in 14 years and for just the second time since 2005.



West Ham will be buoyed by their recent record against the Clarets, having won both meetings between the clubs last season.

Their clash at Turf Moor in February saw the visitors run out 2-0 winners to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture to eight matches.



Meanwhile, Burnley have not claimed all three points against the Hammers since July 2020.

How to follow Burnley vs West Ham

The Hammers will make the trip to Lancashire this Sunday - August 16.

Kick-off at Turf Moor is scheduled for 4pm.

Live commentary will be available on talkSPORT 2 with Max Scott, Adam Bridge and former Scotland striker Chris Iwelumo.



3 West Ham are unbeaten in their last eight matches against the Clarets Credit: Getty

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.



Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

Having been selected for TV coverage, the match will be broadcast on Sky Sports Football and Main Event in the UK.

Burnley vs West Ham team news

New Burnley boss Nicky Hayen is set to be without three first-team players for the visit of West Ham.

Long-term absentees Jordan Beyer and Josh Cullen remain unavailable.

Beyer has not featured in a competitive match since December 2023 due to a serious knee injury.



3 New Burnley boss Hayen will be without three first-team players this weekend Credit: PA

Cullen, meanwhile, is expected to be out until at least October as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury suffered in December.

Jaydon Banel has also been ruled out for several weeks after picking up an issue in training.

Summer signings Ugo Raghouber and Lluc Castell both made their debuts against Notts County last weekend.



Max Alleyne is set to join the club on loan from Manchester City and could do so in time to feature on Sunday.

The Hammers also have injury headaches of their own, with Keiber Lamadrid a doubt this weekend.

Burnley vs West Ham last five meetings February 2026: Burnley 0-2 West Ham November 2025: West Ham 3-2 Burnley March 2024: West Ham 2-2 Burnley November 2023: Burnley 1-2 West Ham April 2022: West Ham 1-1 Burnley

A knee injury suffered in pre-season could see the winger miss two to three weeks of action.

Tomas Soucek is confirmed to miss the trip to Turf Moor after suffering an ankle injury at the World Cup which will keep him out until October.



Recent arrival Joel Veltman made his debut as a late substitute against Pompey and could be in line to start.

Fellow new signing Manor Solomon is also in contention for his league debut.

Sports.title: How Arsenal are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match
Sports.content:
How Arsenal are expected to line up for first 2026/27 Premier League match

Arsenal could be without several key players for the start of their Premier League title defence.

This summer's World Cup saw a number of key Gunners stars involved right up until the final two stages of the tournament.

5 Mikel Arteta has decisions to make with his team selection against Coventry City Credit: AFP

As a result, they have returned late for pre-season following extended time off ahead of the new campaign.

Meanwhile, a potential injury crisis in defence will also limit their options at the beginning of the season.

Despite that, Mikel Arteta is still blessed with options further forward, including two new summer signings.

His side begin the season at home to Championship winners Coventry City on Friday, August 21.

The match is scheduled to kick-off at 8pm, live on talkSPORT, five days after the Community Shield against Manchester City.

So, how will Arsenal line-up for their first match of the new Premier League season?

Arteta's selection headaches

Arteta is only set to be without two first-team players for the visit of Coventry on opening weekend.

Jurrien Timber and William Saliba have already been ruled out of the contest due to injury.

The former has been sidelined with a groin issue since March, which caused him to miss the World Cup for the Netherlands.

Although Timber has returned to light training, the clash with the Sky Blues will come too soon for his return.

5 Timber and Saliba will both be absent for the start of Arsenal's title defence Credit: Getty

As for Saliba, he was forced off with a back injury during France's World Cup final defeat to Spain last month.

The centre-back is currently in the rest stage of his recovery process and is not expected to return to training until after Arsenal's opening fixture.

Elsewhere, David Raya, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Eberechi Eze all returned later for pre-season due to their World Cup exploits.

Having reached the last four, they were handed extended breaks following the tournament.

Whilst Eze and Merino featured against Como in the Gunners' final friendly outing, Zubimendi, Rice and Saka were absent.

Rice battled both injury and illness at the World Cup as England finished third.

5 Rice's World Cup exploits are likely to see him miss the opening fixture Credit: Getty

How will Arsenal line-up on opening day?

Raya made his return to action in the second half against Como, keeping a clean sheet before helping Arsenal win on penalties.

The Gunners' No.1 will retain his place as first-choice this season after winning third successive Premier League golden glove.

It is ahead of him where Arteta has decisions to make, though, with Timber and Saliba both unavailable.

Ben White is expected to start at right-back against Coventry as the only recognised senior player in the position in Timber's absence.

Meanwhile, Cristhian Mosquera will likely partner Gabriel in central defence to avoid having two left-footed centre-backs in the side.

As a result, Piero Hincapie may instead get the nod at left-back ahead of Riccardo Calafiori to begin the season.

5 Summer signing Bruno Guimaraes is in line for his league debut against Coventry Credit: Getty

The Ecuador international started in the role the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in May.

Moving into midfield, Arteta fluctuates between a flat three and two deeper players behind a No.10.

The Arsenal boss has used both systems in pre-season but is known to favour an attacking 4-3-3 when facing weaker sides.

This could see Bruno Guimaraes make his league debut after signing from Newcastle United for £75million.

Both Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze would then join him in an exciting trio for the Gunners.

In attack, Saka's delayed return to pre-season could see fellow England star Noni Madueke start after he featured against Como.

5

On the left, meanwhile, new arrival Christos Tzolis is set to be rewarded for an impressive summer.

The Greece winger has scored once and added two assists in four matches amid speculation surrounding Gabriel Martinelli's future.

Tzolis and Madueke are expected to flank Viktor Gyokeres in the centre-forward role.

Following his own move to north London last summer, Gyokeres ended his debut season with 21 goals in all competitions.

Sports.title: Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state
Sports.content:
Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33 more than a decade after suffering catastrophic brain injuries.

Back in October 2015 Colon, competing as a super-middleweight at the time, suffered a bleed on the brain after taking repeated blows to the back of the head during a contest with America's Terrel Williams in Virginia.

After vomiting and collapsing in the dressing room after his defeat, the Puerto Rican was rushed to hospital before spending 221 days in a coma. The fight with Williams had seen part of his skull collapse as a result of the repeated rabbit punches, which are deemed illegal in the sport.

After emerging from the coma, Colon, once a promising rising star in the ring, was left in a vegetative state with life-altering injuries. He was under the near-constant care of his family.

Colon conquered multiple national amateur championships and won a Youth Pan American gold medal before turning professional.

Colon's dad and former trainer, Richard, announced the heartbreaking news on social media, writing: 'Good morning, everyone. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. He is now in a better place.'

He added: 'Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers.'

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, his family have announced

The Puerto Rican suffered catastrophic brain injuries during a 2015 fight (pictured)

Until that fateful fight almost 11 years ago, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects.

He had established an unblemished 16-0 record with 13 knockouts with many in boxing viewing him as a future star.

Following the bout against Williams, Colon was rushed to the hospital where doctors discovered a subdural hematoma.

He underwent emergency surgery as medics desperately attempted to relieve the swelling in his brain. After spending 221 days in a coma, Colon awoke unable to walk or talk.

Despite the traumatic injuries, just three years ago, Colon had vowed not to throw in the towel.

In an update on his Facebook profile at the time, Colon attempted to speak with his mother and even raised a smile in a moving video.

The post was captioned: 'I will not give up'.

In other clips, the ex-fighter could be seen attending a truck rally with his family, while also appearing to take a positive step in being able to brush his own teeth.

He was left in a vegetative state and was under the near-constant care of his family

Until that fateful fight, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects

His mother also shared a video of her son on his 31st birthday where she gave him a cupcake with a candle on it.

Colon's story is one of the most tragic in boxing history, with former heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder breaking down in tears while discussing it last year.

'We’ve seen what happens, look at Colon. How he got hit, Prichard Colon, correct,' Wilder said.

'This man didn’t have no kids… they don’t understand. Y’all don’t f****** understand what we go through, man.

'And I don’t even know him like that, but I will always be an advocate for us. Because this man will never know what it’s like to be somebody’s father. And that’s one of the most precious things in the world, to be somebody’s father. But he will never be nobody’s father, man.

'Because he got in the ring to support his family but now, his family got to take care of him for the rest of his life.'

Sports.title: Chelsea co-owner 'wants to sell up' as he faces investigation into multi-billion dollar loans - and has already ditched owning the LA Lakers for £9bn
Sports.content:
Chelsea co-owner Mark Walter has expressed an interest in selling his minority stake in the Premier League club, according to reports.

Walter, who has a 12.8 per cent minority stake in BlueCo, the consortium which owns Chelsea, has reportedly hit financial issues which have led to him selling the LA Lakers for a record £9 billion ($12.5bn). This comes less than a year after he bought a majority stake in the NBA franchise.

The US Attorney's Office is currently investigating how billions in loans extended to companies tied to Walter or his conglomerate, TWG Global, have wound up on the books of his insurance companies after passing through a third entity, according to the Wall Street Journal.

'Beyond the Lakers, Walter has also expressed an interest in selling his minority stake in the English Premier League club Chelsea, a person familiar with the matter said,' the report states.

According to Bloomberg, the FBI 'executed at least one search warrant' to seize a mobile phone. In a statement TWG Global, told the Financial Times it is 'aware of and cooperating with the investigation.'

US prosecutors are investigating companies run by Mark Walter, the billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Lakers and the co-owner of Chelsea

Josh Kushner (left), the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, has bought the Lakers from Walter for a record £9bn alongside former Disney CEO Bob Iger

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger appear to have swooped in at a convenient moment for Walter, and the deal for the Lakers is set to be the highest price ever paid for any sports team.

Walter, 66, made his money as one of the founders of bond manager and investment bank Guggenheim Partners in 1999. Beyond Chelsea, Ligue One side Strasbourg, which is also owned by BlueCo, and the LA Lakers, Walter also owns a stake in the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team, is the majority owner of the Los Angeles Sparks women's basketball team, and owns North America's top-level professional women's ice hockey league.

Walter became a minority owner of Chelsea as part of the consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital that completed the takeover of the club in 2022. Walter and Boehly both have a 12.8 per cent minority stake in the club, while Behdad Eghbali, who is co-founder of Clearlake, owns a majority 61.5 per cent.

Walter bought his LA Lakers share, reportedly worth an estimated £7.45bn ($10bn), a previous record, from the Buss family in October 2025.

He said: 'Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honours of my life.

'It has been an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family.'

The deal involving Kushner comes after he was part of the recent controversy surrounding FIFA president Gianni Infantino and an aborted plan to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was expected to lead the proposed investor group for the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

Sports.title: Aston Villa legend and European Cup winner Jimmy Rimmer passes away aged 78
Sports.content:
Aston Villa legend and European Cup winner Jimmy Rimmer passes away aged 78

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa legend Jimmy Rimmer has passed away at the age of 78.

Villa confirmed the passing of Rimmer, who won two European Cups during his career, in a statement on social media.

'Aston Villa is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of European Cup winner Jimmy Rimmer, who has died at the age of 78,' the statement read.

'The thoughts of everyone at the club are with Jimmy's family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.'

Rimmer was described as 'one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation' by Villa and he started the 1982 European Cup final in which the Villans famously triumphed over Bayern Munich.

He made 287 appearances for Villa, having started his career at Manchester United before spending three years at Arsenal.

Former Aston Villa and Man United goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has died aged 78

Rimmer famously had to come off through injury in Aston Villa's 1982 European Cup final triumph over Bayern Munich

The statement continued: 'Rimmer was one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation, and arguably one of the unluckiest when it came to big occasions. Despite collecting two European Cup winner’s medals, he wasn’t on the pitch at the end of either final.

He was on the bench at Wembley in 1968 as Manchester United beat Benfica 4-1 and played for just nine minutes for Villa against Bayern Munich in 1982 before a neck injury forced him to be substituted by Nigel Spink in Rotterdam.

Rimmer was in tears in the dressing room as he received treatment from club doctor David Targett, although he was back in the dug-out in time to witness Peter Withe’s winning goal and join in the post-match celebrations.

Even so, he was one of just five Villa players to figure in the starting line-up in all nine of our European Cup matches that season – and had been one of seven ever-presents in the title-winning campaign of 1980-81.'

The Lancashire lad started his career at Man United while still at school, aged just 15 years old, before turning professional just two years later.

The goalkeeper was primarily a No2 during his 11-year spell at Old Trafford, and was the back up goalkeeper for United's first European Cup win 58 years ago.

His career brought him to Arsenal, where he would finally be promoted to No1 status in his second season at the club.

Rimmer would earn his one and only England cap while on the books at Highbury and won the club's Player of the Year award in 1975.

The shot-stopper then made his name at Villa before ending his career at Swansea City.

Sports.title: 'I want to be an extension of his legacy': New Salford City boss Peter Cklamovski on making Ange Postecoglou 'proud', leading David Beckham's club-wide reboot - and the League Two promotion race
Sports.content:
To most English football fans, Peter Cklamovski is a name that needs some introduction.

The highly rated Australian coach took over as Salford City boss this summer after building an impressive career across continents and in some hugely demanding environments.

He was a long-term assistant to Ange Postecoglou in Australia, Japan and Greece, before striking out on his own, winning plaudits for his attacking, high-energy football and work with young players at Shimizu S-Pulse, Montedio Yamagata and FC Tokyo in Japan. He also impressed with the Malaysia national team.

Now, at 47, he has arrived in League Two as one of the most intriguing EFL appointments in recent years, and with a clear objective – to get Salford promoted after seven seasons in the division.

‘I’ve loved English football from afar and now I’m in the middle of it,’ Cklamovski tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I’m honoured and privileged to be here, and it’s been fantastic so far.’

His relationship with Postecoglou naturally attracts plenty of interest. The pair spent 15 years working together, including a spell in the lower divisions in Greece as the former Tottenham boss built his managerial career.

Salford City appointed Australian coach Peter Cklamovski as their new manager this summer

Cklamovski was a long-term assistant to former Tottenham boss Ange Postecoglou

Together, they won the AFC Asian Cup with Australia and took the Socceroos to the 2014 World Cup. Their partnership was credited with helping reshape coaching standards, methodology and tactical identity in Australia and Asia, and only ended when Cklamovski took the managerial job at Shimizu in 2020.

The pair remain in constant contact, with Postecoglou acting as a mentor and ‘sounding board’ while Cklamovski was applying for the Salford job.

‘Fifteen years with Ange… it’s a long time with anybody,’ says Cklamovski. ‘We’ve got a special connection and synergy. I take a lot from him, and I can't speak highly enough of him.

‘Whatever I’ve done in my career over the last eight years, and however long I've got left, I want it to be an extension of his legacy. That's how much he means to me.

'If we're successful, I know that's going to make him very proud sitting in Saudi Arabia, and hopefully he can do the same in 12 months.’

Cklamovski certainly shares some similarities with his former boss, particularly in his mannerisms and the way he communicates. But his route to English football has been distinctly his own.

‘Mate, this is going to get deep, but for a long time I didn’t really have that aim to get to England as a manager,’ he says. ‘Ange had a motivation to get to English football so as a loyal soldier to him, I pushed hard for that.

‘When I went out on my own, my ambition was to be a dominant manager in Asia. But in the last couple of months, the ambition for me personally, the fire and flame of English football just switched. And here I am.

‘The timing of it was natural. Trust the universe. I’ve got a really strong motivation to do something special with a football club that has great people and an inspiring mentality in the playing group.’

Cklamovski gained rave reviews for his work as a manager in Japan and with Malaysia

He has taken over a Salford side desperate to get promoted from League Two this year

How Cklamovski ended up in the English fourth tier, at a club whose ownership group includes David Beckham and Gary Neville and where Paul Scholes serves as the chief football adviser, is an interesting story.

Its origins date back eight years, when he was working alongside Postecoglou at Yokohama F Marinos, part of the City Football Group.

Salford CEO Gavin Fleig spent 17 years with CFG, including seven as director of talent management, and came across Cklamovski during his time in the Far East.

At the end of a family holiday to the UK earlier this summer, the pair met up. Fleig promised to get in touch if he ever needed a manager.

This was no favour to an old colleague, however. Cklamovski – who didn’t speak to Beckham or Neville during the process – emerged as the outstanding candidate after impressing across various data metrics and during the interview process.

‘The aim is to chase promotions and that resonates with me,’ he says. ‘I'm not afraid of that. I have a strong belief we can achieve it with special people and play a brand of football that's going to entertain our fans and bring pride and excitement to the Salford community.’

Scholes had to Google Cklamovski as he didn’t know who he was, but was particularly impressed, although Salford’s decision to appoint a manager with no experience of English football is undoubtedly a risk.

That move came after the club sacked Karl Robinson despite only missing out on automatic promotion on the final day of last season, before they lost to Notts County in the play-off final.

The hierarchy admitted the decision to part company with Robinson was a difficult one. But with Salford’s budget understood to have increased this season, the club are determined to finally make the step up to League One.

Cklamovski intends to build on Robinson's work, rather than rip everything up and start again.

‘Whatever sort of team you take over, you can’t stand still,’ he says. ‘We've got the benefit of the work done over the years, especially last year, and we’ve used that as a foundation. But you’ve got to go to another level. We’ll use the heartache from last year as motivation as well.’

Salford missed out on automatic promotion last season before losing in the play-off final

Salford, whose ownership group includes Gary Neville and David Beckham, have reverted to their traditional orange colours ahead of a big season for the club

His arrival at Moor Lane coincides with a significant season of change for Salford.

The club have increased their playing budget, reverted to their traditional orange colours as part of a rebrand in which Beckham played a key role, improved their Man United-owned Littleton Road training ground and overhauled their medical department.

There have also been statement signings, including Millwall striker Macaulay Langstaff, the League Two Golden Boot winner in 2023-24, and Doncaster Rovers winger Luke Molyneux, who was named in the division’s Team of the Season in 2024-25.

‘It’s a sign of the club’s ambition,’ Cklamovski says. ‘But it also shows the commitment to building something special long-term. We’ve made some great signings but there's a super core group here as well, and that's exciting.’

Salford begin their league campaign at Barnet on Saturday after losing on penalties to Shrewsbury in the EFL Cup last week.

It promises to be the first proper acid test of Cklamovski’s reign – and whether his aggressive style can translate into the results and entertainment he has promised supporters.

‘We want to play a brand of football that's going to make every Salford fan and everyone at the club proud and excited,’ he says. 'We want to have a goalscoring mentality, but we'll also have a real strong mentality to roll our sleeves up and keep clean sheets.

‘We've got to stay humble, work hard, and commit to that. Some really good work has started, but there's a lot more work to do.’

Sports.title: Jimmy Rimmer and Nigel Spink interview: I thought 1982 would be my finest hour - but it's a team game, not Jimmy Rimmer's game
Sports.content:
This interview was originally published in May 2024. We are republishing it now after the passing of Jimmy Rimmer on Friday, at the age of 78.

Jimmy Rimmer reaches out a hand and apologises for the state of his grip. 'Like the hands you see in horror films,' he says drily, running a finger along some of the artificial joints.

'It's not pretty is it? That's plastic in there, and that, and that's been frozen,' explains the 76-year-old former Manchester United, Arsenal and Aston Villa goalkeeper. 'At least I'm still alive,' he laughs. 'They only gave me two days to live, you know.'

This seems like a good place to start. Rimmer was living in Vancouver when he suffered a heart attack, collapsing as he climbed out of his Jeep on a routine trip to the bank.

Hospital staff told his three children they would keep him alive on life support machine until they had a chance to fly to Canada and bid their father farewell but, by the time they landed, there were signs of life.

'Eleven days in a coma and just like that I came out,' recalls Rimmer. 'People ask me what it was like. All I know is it was dark.'

Ex-Aston Villa goalkeepers Jimmy Rimmer (left) and Nigel Spink (right) hold the European Cup

Rimmer (left) was substituted for Spink (right) just 10 minutes into the 1982 European Cup final

Rimmer (left) had suffered an injury before the game that saw him leave the pitch 10 minutes in

Sixteen years later, he is enjoying a pint in a bustling pub on the outskirts of Swansea retracing the twists of his brilliant if underappreciated career.

'I played for the best club in the north, the best in the south, the best in the Midlands and the best in Wales,' he likes to say, but he never cared to boast much at the time.

He comes from the strong and silent mould, much like his mentor Harry Gregg, the Manchester United and Northern Ireland goalkeeper and reluctant hero of the Munich disaster.

Towards the end of his playing career at Old Trafford, Gregg dispensed sagely advice and coaching tips to young 'keepers competing to be his permanent successor.

'Catch the ball, get some shape in your hands, Harry would tell us. Cover your near post. They're not so good at the near post these days.'

Rimmer came through the ranks with George Best, David Sadler and John Aston. Together they were Youth Cup winners in 1964 and European champions within four years.

Among his fondest memories of United's triumph against Benfica, when he was an unused substitute at Wembley Stadium, is the celebration banquet when he and Best sat together with their parents.

It was Gregg who convinced him a loan move into Division Four with Swansea was a good idea, and who told Arsenal scout Gordon Clark to sign him in April 1974.

Ex-Man United goalkeeper Harry Gregg would impart knowledge to up-and-coming players

Gregg (left) apparently convinced Rimmer that a loan move to join Swansea was a good idea

Rimmer's Arsenal debut came in a 1-0 win at Liverpool and accused Alan Ball of a wind-up as he was offered a choice of prawn cocktail or smoked salmon on the bus journey home.

'I said, "what do you mean?" At Man United the bus driver would go and get fish and chips and there's two fellas asking me what starter I'd like, whether I want steak or chicken and red or white wine.

'I'm looking at Bally because we're playing bridge and I'm the new one, and I think they're taking the p*** here but they weren't. No more driving to the chip shop. That's why they're call The Arsenal. It's nothing but the best. And I'd come from Man United.'

Rimmer grew in stature when Bob Wilson retired at the end of that season and, once elevated to number one, missed only three games in three years.

There came England recognition albeit only one cap, against Italy in 1976, and he remembers coming in at number 20 when Gordon Banks ranked the world's top goalkeepers in a newspaper column.

'I was over the moon,' says Rimmer. 'People told me how good I was but I didn't always realise. I was very shy and quiet at one time. I'd go into my own world when I made a mistake. Harry Gregg would say, "Oh you're the only one who ever made a mistake are you".

'We all make mistakes. I used to hold them in and think about them for too long. You can't go around telling people about all the great saves you made.

Rimmer (third from front) had played in teams with Bobby Charlton (front) and George Best (second from front)

Rimmer ranked in the world's top 20 goalkeepers when Gordon Banks (pictured) was the best

'I hate to say it but I could sit here happy in my own company. I could sit here and have a beer and people would think I wasn't happy. They'd say, "that quiet fella in the corner used to be famous."'

Perhaps the perception is enhanced events of the European Cup final in 1982.

It ought to have been Rimmer's finest hour but turned out be one of football's cruellest twists of fate.

He had rejected a new deal at Arsenal and an offer to join Ipswich Town to sign for Aston Villa, where he thrived under Ron Saunders. They got along, played a lot of golf together, and shared an outlook. Men of action, not liable to waste words.

Rimmer missed only one game in five years as Villa won the title for the only time in the last 114 years, and then forged into Europe, reaching the final with seven clean sheets in eight games.

His heroics against Dynamo Berlin have gone down as one of his finest displays.

In the final league game of the season, however, just five days before the final against Bayern Munich in Rotterdam, he came out for a cross, caught it, collided with Bob Latchford of Swansea, spun over and crashed down onto the back of his neck.

'Next day my shoulder was terrible,' says Rimmer. 'The doctor wasn't sure the jabs would work but Tony Barton wanted me to play so we tried to make sure nobody knew.

'I had injections in my neck and my shoulder. Cortisone takes pain away but eight or nine minutes into the game, I knew there was no chance. You've got to have a goalkeeper who can make saves. I couldn't lift my arm.

'You've got to be a man, there was a decision to make. I had to make it as a senior player. I could've stayed on. We'd worked hard to get there and we wanted to win. It's a team game not Jimmy Rimmer's game. I cried in the dressing room.

'The good thing was that I think I made the right decision. The lad came on and was magnificent. Full credit to him.'

Despite Rimmer's absence, Aston Villa went on to win the 1982 European Cup final

Peter Withe scored the only goal of the game against Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich

Villa captain Dennis Mortimer hoisted the trophy high into the air after the 1-0 victory

Nigel Spink had joined Villa as a teenager from non-league Chelmsford City, at first as an understudy to John Burridge, then to Rimmer when he arrived from Arsenal, six months later.

He waited almost three years for his debut, a defeat at Nottingham Forest on Boxing Day 1979 and another two-and-a-half for his second appearance, when Rimmer trudged off in the European Cup final.

'Jimmy was so consistent he never missed a game and my education came from watching him train and play,' recalls 65-year-old Spink. 'He had spent two years winning the league and getting us to the final of the European Cup and then missed the real cherry on top.

Spink made his second senior appearance for Aston Villa during the European Cup final

'I felt for him in that situation. Almost guilty when the dust settled. He hadn't been able to play in a final he deserved to play in.'

As he went on, Spink turned the bench and said, 'I hope my Mum's got the telly on'. In fact, she had, and her son rose to the occasion with outstanding performance. Villa kept another clean sheet and won 1-0, the goal by Peter Withe.

'The basis of my performance was hundreds of reserve games for Villa over a five-year period so I carried on as if it was a reserve game and was able to deal with what the Germans threw at me.

'A couple of saves built confidence and then, just as I'm starting to feel good, Karlheinz Rummenigge did this amazing overhead kick that shaved the outside of the post. As Gordon Cowans ran past me to pick the ball up I said to him, "I'm not sure I'm meant to be here".'

It was a life-changing night for Spink as he kept Bayern at bay.

'When I ran on the pitch in Rotterdam, I doubt even the Villa supporters knew who I was. I'd never played. Only the real fanatics would've known my name. When we got back, everywhere I went I got recognised. Certainly around Birmingham. People just wanted to buy you drinks and were happy for you.'

Spink took the European Cup to his native Essex where his parents threw a garden party with the trophy sitting proudly on the front lawn for neighbours to come by and pose for photos. 'There were kids sitting in it, can you imagine that now?'

Spink (right) said that he had 'felt for Jimmy in that situation' after he had been substituted

The goalkeeper (left) said he treated the final 'like a reserves match' and had made a few saves that built up his confidence

Villa did manage to lose the trophy while it was in their possession. 'It went missing from Lions Club fans' night and, so the story goes, was handed in at Sheffield police station,' says Spink.

Rimmer, only the second player after Saul Malatrasi of Milan and Inter, to win the European Cup with different clubs, was restored to the Villa team at the start of the following season but had signed for Swansea by the end.

Spink took over as number one and held the position for many years, making 460 appearances before moving to West Bromwich Albion. Like Rimmer, he won one England cap, against Australia in Melbourne.

His last Villa game came as a substitute in midfield at Queens Park Rangers, on a day when Lee Hendrie was sent off on his debut, and his favourite Villa Park memories come from European games.

Beating Barcelona to claim the Super Cup in January 1983 and the home leg of a European Cup quarter-final against Juventus, two months later, when Spink waited in vain for Dino Zoff's shirt.

'I sent my jersey into their dressing room and after about an hour standing around outside I knocked on the door and asked for Zoff's jersey,' says Spink. 'The kitman went back in and came out with a new jersey, still in the packet. That was a bit disappointing.'

Although there is a happier tale of swapped shirts from Spink, who brought the shirt of Bayern goalkeeper Manfred Muller back from Rotterdam and over time came to wish he still had his own.

Spink recounted how he was able to obtain his original jersey from the 1982 final (pictured) from Bayern Munich's club museum

When he contacted Bayern's museum to ask if they wanted Muller's shirt back, he discovered they were in possession of his original from 1982 and were more than happy to swap back.

Spink and his wife called in at Munich on his way back from a skiing holiday in Austria. 'They treated us like Gods,' he says. 'They treated us better than Villa do. I think Bayern have more respect for our achievement than Villa.

'They came out with this presentation box, lined with tissue paper and there was my shirt folded neatly with half a dozen pictures from the night from their archives on top.

'My wife kicked me under the table because Manfred's shirt was in a crumpled Sainsbury's carrier bag. I apologised but they didn't seem to mind, and we had a chuckle.

'It was emotional to see my shirt again. There was no chance of me getting it on but my daughter pulled it on and posed for some photographs. I loved that Le Coq Sportif strip. That jersey is my favourite out of all the ones ever I wore for Villa.'

He said it was 'emotional' to see his Cup final shirt again, adding it was 'his favourite Villa top'

Members of the 1982 European Cup winning team were given a guard of honour as Villa celebrated the 40th anniversary of their triumph back in 2022

Rimmer is not one for undue sentiment. He finished playing at Swansea, where he started coaching and had two spells as caretaker manager before moving to China.

'I went for three months and stayed for years,' he says of his time coaching the goalkeepers in the Chinese national team and later Dalian Wanda, who became Dalian Shide. 'If they like you, you'll stay there a long time. If they don't like you, they'll give you great money and say goodbye.'

For much of that time, he lived rent-free in a penthouse suite of the Shangri-La in Beijing. 'The first thing I learned to respect their culture. That's why I think I lasted.'

Eventually, Rimmer left China for Canada and returned to South Wales after his heart attack to be closer to his son David, the source of what he calls his only footballing regret, when he decided against offering him a scholarship during his time as Swansea's youth team manager.

'He was a centre-half with great feet,' says Rimmer. 'I decided to keep a spot spare in case we found someone else. I should have given my son that position. It was my mistake.'

Unai Emery's side are now one win away from their first European Cup final since 1982

Both Spink and Rimmer will also know that goalkeeper Emi Martinez is struggling with an injury

David joined Walsall, then Birmingham City but missed home and was soon back in Swansea, where he played amateur football including a long spell at Garden Village, where he has recently been manager before stepping aside to focus on his courier business.

Rimmer senior often be spotted following the Swans, a regular at games and an occasional speaker in their match-day lounges. He rarely makes it to Aston Villa but supporters all his former clubs from afar.

It will not have escaped him or Spink that Villa are one win from their first European final since 1982 and the established first-choice goalkeeper Emi Martinez is struggling with an injury.

Sports.title: Arsenal hold talks over signing Victor Osimhen amid interest in Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri - as Barcelona prepare fresh bid for Rodri: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Arsenal's Osimhen interest

Arsenal have discussed signing Victor Osimhen during talks with Galatasaray over the potential sales of Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri.

Galatasaray made a £38.5million verbal offer for Martinelli, but the 25-year-old Brazilian is reluctant to leave London.

Nwaneri, 19, meanwhile, is assessing his options and, as it stands, talks for Nigeria striker Osimhen have not progressed.

Victor Osimhen's name was discussed by Arsenal transfer chiefs this summer

Martinelli has also had tentative interest from Paris Saint-Germain in recent weeks, but the French side have now turned their attention to Ajax’s Mika Godts, 21.

England Under-21 international Nwaneri was frustrated with a lack of game time last season, but has interest from AC Milan, Fulham, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund, among others.

Arsenal are also in talks with West Ham over the £3m sale of winger Reiss Nelson, and Napoli want striker Gabriel Jesus.

There is interest from Hamburg for Fabio Vieira, and fellow midfielder Martin Zubimendi is on the radar of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid.

Barca prepare next Rodri offer

Barcelona are drafting a new proposal for Manchester City midfielder Rodri after their second offer was rejected. City are holding for closer £68m for the Spain captain.

Rodri was spotted by fans travelling back to Liverpool airport on a Ryanair flight from Madrid on Thursday evening.

City have rejected two bids from Barcelona for the midfielder, the second of which was around £55m.

Rodri is waiting on Barcelona and Man City to agree a fee for his move back to Spain

Hammers smash transfer record for Engels

West Ham have agreed a Championship record transfer fee worth £22million for Celtic midfielder Arne Engels.

The Belgium international is due to undergo a medical in London today with the Hammers who have a long-held interest in the 22-year-old and had previously had two bids rejected by Celtic last month.

The previous record transfer fee is £17.5m paid by Ipswich Town to Nordsjaelland for Sindre Walle Egeli.

Marseille move for Perri

Marseille are continuing talks for Leeds goalkeeper Lucas Perri.

The Brazilian, who joined Leeds from Lyon, had been lined up for a loan to Torino and was even scheduled for medical but Marseille have been pushing this week to convince him of their project after selling Geronimo Rulli to Manchester City.

Rulli was bought as cover after James Trafford was sold to Leeds, who are closing on an £8.2m deal for Borussia Monchengladbach centre back Nico Elvedi. The Switzerland international, 29, can also play at right back.

Meanwhile, Marseille have also enquired about Arsenal forward Reiss Nelson.

The 26-year-old has been discussing a £3m move to West Ham but is unsure about dropping to the Championship.

Everton keen on Wheatley

Manchester United and Everton are continuing discussions over the transfer of Ethan Wheatley.

The 20-year-old striker is viewed as one for the future by Everton but will be able to have an impact in the first team.

The England Under-20 international is 6ft 3in and regularly clocks 36km/h in sprints. He has been on loan at Northampton Town and Bradford City in recent seasons and was a prolific scorer through youth levels at United.

United winger Ethan Williams has joined Peterborough for an undisclosed fee. United’s deal also includes add-ons, a 50 per cent sell-on clause, a buy-back option and matching rights.

Spence ready for Italian job

Tottenham full back Djed Spence arrived in Milan last night ahead of his £26m move to Inter.

The 26-year-old has started his medical tests at the CONI Sports Medicine Institute this morning.

.@Inter, Spence è arrivato al CONI per l’idoneità sportiva pic.twitter.com/vYZESpNdfX — Gianluca Di Marzio (@DiMarzio) August 14, 2026

Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr is emerging as a target for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League. The 23-year-old will be allowed to leave and has been the subject of interest from Brentford and Aston Villa as well as other European sides.

Juventus have revived talks for Spurs keeper Guglielmo Vicario while defender Cristian Romero will have his medical with Atletico Madrid tomorrow.

Spurs remain in talks for Manchester City winger Savinho and Cody Gakpo of Liverpool. City’s Omar Marmoush is also on their list.

Badiashile set for Napoli switch

Napoli have agreed a deal with Chelsea to sign defender Benoit Badiashile on an initial loan for £2.5m that could rise to £3.4m with an option to buy permanently for around £23m.

Celtic are closing in on a loan for Chelsea full back Landon Emenalo.

Where there's a Will, there's a way

Will Smallbone has emerged as a target for West Brom. The 26-year-old midfielder is a free agent after leaving Southampton.

The Republic of Ireland international has a number of options but Albion have emerged as they are losing Alex Mowatt to Derby.

Benda heading to Forest

Nottingham Forest are signing Fulham goalkeeper Steven Benda on a free transfer. He is due for a medical today.

Tiger Tim

Hull have formalised their interest in Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam with an offer understood to be in excess of £15million. The 23-year-old has a year left on contract.

Leeds forward Joe Gelhardt has completed his medical at Hull ahead of his £4.5million move.

So Burnley bound

Brazilian side Palmeiras have signed Fabio So from Burnley.

Zaha returns home

Free agent Wilfried Zaha is training alone at former club Crystal Palace while he searches for a new club.

Howell heads to Leicester

Brighton midfielder Harry Howell has joined Leicester on a season's loan.

SATURDAY: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon

FRIDAY: Rodri tells Real Madrid he wishes to join Barcelona

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher identifies 'huge problem' at Liverpool which means they WON'T compete for the Premier League title - despite there being 'too much quality'!
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher identifies 'huge problem' at Liverpool which means they WON'T compete for the Premier League title - despite there being 'too much quality'!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher has expressed his concern over the club's midfield heading into the new season.

The Reds are now under the management of Andoni Iraola after a difficult campaign in 2025-26 where they came fifth, a finish that resulted in Arne Slot being sacked.

So far this summer, the club have added winger Victor Munoz and Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo, while Jeremy Jacquet has joined up with the squad after his move from Rennes was agreed in January.

Iraola's side are yet to strengthen in midfield though, leaving them with the same options as last season - and Carragher believes that could be a key issue.

'The midfield for me is still a huge problem for Liverpool,' he told The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet. 'I haven’t watched all the pre-season games, but I watched the last two against decent opposition - it was Leeds and then Monaco.

'And the problem Liverpool had last season was there was space everywhere in midfield. That has not gone away at all.

Jamie Carragher has expressed his concern over Liverpool's midfield ahead of the new season

Carragher highlighted the area as a 'huge problem' for new Reds boss Andoni Iraola

'That’s only going to get bigger with the deployment of [Dominik] Szoboszlai in midfield.

'It looks like they’re going to play him, rather than as a number 10, almost as a central midfield player alongside [Ryan] Gravenberch and that is just pure box-to-box.'

Carragher went on to call for Liverpool to sign an 'out-and-out number six' to provide more solidity and depth.

The former defender also felt Iraola had to find a better way to get the balance right in midfield, and admitted that while there is plenty of energy among his options available, that could lead to issues.

'I look at that midfield three and I worry,' he added. 'When you name six or seven of Liverpool’s players, you can’t say they’re not top players.

'You can’t say Gravenberch is not a really good player, or [Florian] Wirtz, or [Dominik] Szoboszlai.

'But as a midfield three, I look at that and think, oh no, there’s almost too much quality, but they all want to go and play and run. And even in pre-season, the space is coming through the middle.'

Having won the title in 2024-25, last season did prove to be a significant drop off for the Reds, and they have also since lost both Mohamed Salah and Ibrahima Konate.

Carragher said the decision to play Dominik Szoboszlai as a No 8 leaves the team too open

So far in pre-season they have won two and lost two, and Iraola's side conclude their preparations against Como this weekend.

But despite the potential of a new manager bounce and more signings in the market, Carragher felt that the weaknesses he highlighted would ultimately hold them back this year.

'I struggle to see how that midfield three [of Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai & Ryan Gravenberch] - who are all individually really good players - is a midfield three that gets Liverpool back to competing for the title,' he said.

'I’m not sure about that at all.'

Sports.title: Declan Rice kicks back with James Corden in Sardinia as Arsenal star enjoys luxury yacht break with comedian and West Ham legend Mark Noble ahead of new season
Sports.content:
Declan Rice kicks back with James Corden in Sardinia as Arsenal star enjoys luxury yacht break with comedian and West Ham legend Mark Noble ahead of new season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

After a gruelling season, both mentally and physically, followed by an intense run to the semi-finals of the World Cup, Arsenal star Declan Rice has been making the most of every moment of his downtime.

Rice racked up an impressive 69 appearances for club and country last season, helping Arsenal secure their first Premier League title in 22 years and reach their first Champions League final in two decades, where they were beaten by Paris Saint-Germain on penalties.

He also played a crucial role in England's third-place finish at the World Cup under Thomas Tuchel, despite being hampered by injury and illness throughout the tournament.

Sharing 12 photographs on Instagram alongside the caption 'peace', Rice looked relaxed and sun-kissed as he enjoyed a luxurious break.

One image showed the 27-year-old alongside James Corden and former West Ham team-mate Mark Noble at a high-end Asian fusion restaurant called Nammos Baja, on the coast of Italy's Sardinia.

Another featured Rice arm-in-arm with Noble, who now serves as sporting director of the Championship club, with a huge yacht behind them.

Rice was pictured alongside James Corden and former West Ham team-mate Mark Noble at a high-end Asian fusion restaurant called Nammos Baja, on the coast of Italy's Sardinia

Rice shared a picture arm-in-arm with Noble, who now serves as sporting director of the Championship club, with a huge yacht behind them

The midfielder has been enjoying family time too, pictured alongside three-year-old son Jude

Rice reportedly struck up a friendship with Corden during England's Euro 2020 campaign, when Noble took him to watch one of the games.

Rice also shared a picture alongside Noble taken in front of a huge cruise liner with a helicopter perched on top, as well as a selfie from the driver's seat of a jet ski.

The midfielder has been enjoying family time too, with three-year-old son Jude pictured kicking a football on a golf course and trying his hand at fishing.

It will have provided the perfect tonic after a physically demanding summer that saw Rice limp out of England's World Cup group-stage clash with Ghana with heavy strapping on his left calf.

It later emerged that Rice had been suffering from a neural issue affecting his hamstring and lower back, which left him bed-bound for three days before England's quarter-final victory over Norway.

After being substituted at half-time against Erling Haaland's Norway, Rice returned to play 82 minutes of England's semi-final defeat by Argentina.

It wasn't until the Three Lions' bronze-medal win over France that he appeared to be back to his best, opening the scoring with a stunning third-minute strike before completing the full 90 minutes of the remarkable 10-goal thriller.

Either way, Mikel Arteta will be keen not to rush Rice back ahead of schedule, given the importance of keeping one of his key players fit throughout the campaign.

Rice also posted snaps of a huge cruise liner, a helicopter and a selfie from the driver's seat of a jet ski

Rice is now easing his way back in after watching Arsenal's friendly against Como in north London on Wednesday

The Arsenal manager has already praised Rice's mindset on his return to pre-season training.

'We have three different pre-seasons with different groups, but the most important thing is the attitude,' Arteta said at the end of July.

'When I speak to Declan Rice, he is already saying, "OK, if I come this day, then I can play then."

'That is much more powerful than the programme. We want to adapt to the context, which is different.'

Rice is now easing his way back in after watching Arsenal's friendly against Como in north London on Wednesday.

The Gunners begin their competitive campaign against Manchester City in the Community Shield at Cardiff's Principality Stadium this weekend.

As has become customary in recent years, the Premier League champions will then kick off the new league season on the Friday night.

For Arsenal, that means a home clash with newly promoted Coventry City, managed by former Chelsea midfielder Frank Lampard, at the Emirates Stadium on 21 August.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson's off-track life – marriage plans, behaviour remark, serious injury
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson's off-track life – marriage plans, behaviour remark, serious injury

Keely Hodgkinson is the face of British athletics and the star of the European Championships in Birmingham, where she will try to beat the long-standing 800m world record on Friday night

View 4 Images Keely Hodgkinson is looking to become a three-time European champion in the 800m event (Image: Steven Paston/PA Wire)

Keely Hodgkinson has become one of the biggest names in British athletics, with her achievements on the track matched by a personality that has made her hugely popular away from it.

‌



The Olympic 800m champion will be back under the spotlight on Friday evening when she lines up in the women's 800m final at the European Championships in Birmingham, with a third successive title potentially within her grasp and the world record in her sights.

‌



At just 24, Hodgkinson has already packed an extraordinary amount into her career. Her gold medal-winning performance at the Paris 2024 Olympics cemented her status among the sport's elite, but her journey has also included painful injuries and difficult spells away from the track.

‌



Here, Mirror Sport looks at some of the biggest revelations surrounding the 2026 Sports Personality of the Year, exploring everything from her future personal ambitions to her inspiring resilience.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

What time is Keely Hodgkinson competing today? How to watch Team GB star READ MORE :

Keely Hodgkinson shows her class in BBC interview as result changed after appeal READ MORE :

Marriage admission

For all the success Hodgkinson has enjoyed professionally, she has made it clear that there are ambitions in her personal life that matter just as much. During an appearance on Welsh sprinter Jeremiah Azu's YouTube channel, she revealed that starting a family is among her biggest goals for the next decade.

‌



Asked what she wanted to achieve over the next 10 years, Hodgkinson admitted that marriage and motherhood were high on her list. "Mine is I'd like to start a family and get married. That's a big thing for me," she said.

She even gave herself a personal target, adding: "I'll be 34, I'd like to think I'd had a baby by then and I really look forward to that point of my life at some point."

View 4 Images Keely Hodgkinson says she wants to start in family in the next few years (Image: Domenico Cippitelli/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Her love life has previously been complicated by the demands of being an elite athlete. Hodgkinson was in a relationship with a fellow athlete for three years before the pair split in early 2024, with the pressures of a long-distance relationship proving difficult as their careers took them between Texas, Italy and London.

"Because I do what I do and put that first, we could go weeks, months and not see each other," she told The Times. "I'm not really interested in dating right now. I've never been on the apps. I like meeting people in real life."

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

‌



Injury that left her unable to walk

Hodgkinson's remarkable ability to make the 800m appear almost effortless has sometimes disguised the physical punishment involved in competing at the highest level.

That was evident in July when she arrived at a Diamond League meeting in Eugene, Oregon, with her knees heavily strapped. She had suffered a serious fall just days earlier, with the damage leaving her struggling to move before eventually finishing second behind Lilian Odira.

Her condition became clear after the race, when Hodgkinson revealed just how badly the fall had affected her. "It's shocking, to be honest," she admitted. "Four days ago I couldn't even walk, so I guess I should take that into consideration but I wanted a lot more than that."

‌



View 4 Images Hodgkinson endured injury problems after winning Olympic gold at Paris 2024 (Image: Mustafa Ciftci/Anadolu via Getty Images)

The Olympic champion later posted a photograph on Instagram from a medical room, showing the bruising across her knees. Alongside the image, she wrote the determined caption: "Forward motion". The photograph prompted a wave of support from fellow athletes and fans, who praised Hodgkinson for competing despite the severity of her injuries.

It was another setback during an inconsistent period for the 800m star. She had already been forced to withdraw from the 400m final at the UK Athletics Championships in June after suffering what she described as a "little twinge".

‌



Despite the disruption, Hodgkinson's ambitions have remained unchanged. One of her biggest targets is still to break the 800m world record, which has stood since Jarmila Kratochvilova set the mark in 1983.

Behaviour comments

Hodgkinson has also attracted considerable praise for the person she is away from the athletics track, with World Athletics president and Team GB legend Sebastian Coe among those to have spoken particularly highly of her.

View 4 Images Seb Coe has lavished praise on Keely Hodgkinson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



During an appearance on the UNTAPPED podcast, the two-time Olympic 1500m champion called Hodgkinson "probably the most authentic person I currently know."

Coe recalled bumping into her at a Manchester restaurant while she was celebrating her birthday. Despite being only days away from winning her world indoor title, Hodgkinson was simply enjoying a normal night out.

"What you see with Keely is what you get. She is very funny, she's totally driven, but she puts things in perspective," Coe said. He went on to praise Hodgkinson for maintaining a sense of grounded normality despite her extraordinary sporting talent and fiercely competitive nature.

Article continues below

"She's just completely normal, but she is incredibly well talented. She's got a great coaching team around her. I'm probably going to lose whatever fan base I've got left in the south of England, but she's absolutely rooted to the north of England and that for me counts for a lot in life."

Sports.title: Count Binface compares Clacton by-election to CARABAO CUP after winning 26 per cent of vote
Sports.content:
Count Binface compares Clacton by-election to CARABAO CUP after winning 26 per cent of vote

Count Binface came up against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage in the Clacton by-election, with all other major parties pulling out.

View 2 Images Count Binface has compared the by-election to the Carabao Cup after losing to Nigel Farage. (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

Count Binface has sent a warning to Nigel Farage, comparing his defeat in the Clacton by-election to the first leg of a Carabao Cup tie. Farage, leader of Reform UK, won the election with 22,239 votes.

‌



His main rival, a parody candidate, Count Binface earned 9.455 votes, 26 percent of the overall votes in a 44.4 percent turnout. Despite his victory, Farage did not attend the results declaration.

‌



Instead, he hosted his own 'Farage Fest' party. In a speech, he said: "I've been advised tonight by Essex Police that there is an organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result that will take place in a few hours' time."

‌



Cristiano Ronaldo married in front of just FOUR witnesses and signed pre-nup READ MORE :

Paul Pogba's wife responds to retirement demand as Monaco contract set to be ripped up READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The by-election, which is estimated to have cost £250,000, has been labelled as a gimmick by all other major parties, who boycotted the race, leaving Count Binface as Farage's main rival The election came amid scrutiny over a £5million gift he received just before the 2024 general election.

Once Farage has been sworn in as an MP, an investigation into the gift is expected to open. If he is found to be in serious breach of the rules, then he could face a possible suspension, which would lead to another by-election in Clacton.

‌



It's something that Count Binface referred to when speaking to Sky News after Farage claimed victory. "You've just said at the beginning of this interview that Nigel Farage is claiming victory," he said.

"Well in that case it's going to be a two-legged match, like the Carabao Cup or the Cold War, because we're going to be back in a few weeks aren't we? We'll see what happens then."

View 2 Images Count Binface after the declaration of the Clacton by-election results. (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

‌



Speaking before the election about the resources put into it by Reform UK, Count Binface added: "Whether he's scared of me, you need to ask Nigel that, but I have noticed just how hard Reform have been campaigning against an alien space warrior with a Ceefax fetish who only eight weeks ago scored 0.2% [of the vote share] in Makerfield.

"So yeah, it's a curious... But I respect it, and I'm rather flattered."

When asked what a good result would be, he said: "Well look, a single vote, one precious vote, imagine one human like you going into that voting booth, getting the stubby pencil out, and choosing Binface instead of Farage.

Article continues below

"Just give yourself a moment to think about that. Anybody deciding they would rather vote for me to be Member of Parliament than Nigel Farage is a win. Now, you magnify that every single time there's an X for Binface and it mounts up, and it mounts up, and it mounts up.

"And I'll be interested to see the headlines you guys write with the number of people, percentage-wise, who make that decision."

Sports.title: Man Utd £42.7m boost as Liverpool make Ibrahim Mbaye decision
Sports.content:
Man Utd £42.7m boost as Liverpool make Ibrahim Mbaye decision

Manchester United have been linked with a move for Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye in the final weeks of the transfer window.

View 2 Images Manchester United and Liverpool have shown a transfer interest in Ibrahim Mbaye. (Image: Michael Reaves, Getty Images)

Liverpool have reportedly pulled out of the race to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye, providing a potential transfer boost to rivals Manchester United. Both Liverpool and United have been credited with an interest in the Senegal international.

‌



But they are not alone, with Bayern Munich, Porto, RB Leipzig, Bayer Leverkusen, Borussia Dortmund, Roma and Aston Villa all said to have made enquiries with PSG over his availability. It does, however, seem that Liverpool have dropped their interest, due to the cost involved.

‌



It's reported by Fabrizio Romano on his YouTube channel that the club have held talks with agent Jorge Mendes over the possible transfer, but stepped away from a possible deal after being told it would cost €200 million (£171m) to sign both Mbaye and key target Bradley Barcola. Liverpool remain in talks with PSG over a deal for Barcola.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

While a deal for the Frenchman would account for the bulk of the figure quoted, reports suggest PSG are seeking between €40m-€50m (£34.2m-£42.7m) for Mbaye. It's a valuation Liverpool considers excessive, prompting them to drop their interest.

It's a development United could look to capitalise on, particularly given PSG's most recent transfer activity. The Athletic reports that the European champions have agreed a £42.7m fee with Barcelona to sign Ferran Torres.

‌



His arrival at Les Parc des Princes is only set to further limit Mbaye's opportunities on the pitch and, consequently, make PSG more willing to consider a sale. AS reports that the club might even be prepared to approve a loan departure.

View 2 Images Ibrahim Mbaye is the subject of interest from several clubs in the transfer window. (Image: Jean Catuffe, Getty Images)

The winger remained on the bench throughout PSG's 2-1 European Super Cup triumph over Aston Villa on Wednesday night. This came despite him netting the team's goal in the 1-1 pre-season stalemate against United the weekend before.

‌



Mbaye featured 31 times across all competitions last season, finding the net three times and registering two assists. Yet of those outings, only 11 saw him named in the starting XI.

He predominantly operates on the right flank, but is also capable of featuring on the left. Should United succeed in securing his signature, he will link up with the likes of Marcus Rashford, Bryan Mbeumo, Amad, Patrick Dorgu and Shea Lacey as wide attacking options for Michael Carrick this season.

United return to pre-season duty on Saturday when they face AC Milan (3.45pm kick-off), a fixture which could witness Rashford making his comeback for the club after returning from a loan spell with Barcelona.
