World.title: Should Croatia Send SRUUK Messages to Tourists Before Danger Strikes?
World.content:
August the 14th, 2026 – Should Croatia send out SRUUK messages to tourists before danger strikes? With more and more incidents of mountain, sea and other rescues taking place, some believe the country be doing more to warn visitors of potential risks.

Four Portuguese nationals recently went missing at sea after strong bura winds took control of their 1.5 metre inflatable boat. Index reports that this is one incident in an increasingly long list of issues that take place every single summer. From flip flop-donning “hikers” on Biokovo to people trying to cross the Adriatic to Italy on an inflatable flamingo, there’s never a drama-free tourist season in this regard.

The question for some is whether Croatia could be doing more, such as sending out SRUUK messages to tourists about specific dangers they may face during their stay. The latest case of the Portuguese tourists being swept away has once again raised the question of how well tourists are actually warned about the dangers of a strong and stormy bura. This is especially true in the area of the Velebit Channel, where rescue operations for people blown away from the shore by the wind are commonplace during the season.

sruuk messages specifically for bura winds

A similar case occurred at the end of July, when the bura carried a foreign national on a SUP board from Karlobag across the Velebit Channel all the way to Pag. After a multi-hour night-time operation, the Croatian Mountain Rescue Service (HGSS) found him uninjured on an inaccessible part of the Pag coast.

Because of the frequent occurrence of such cases, an inquiry was sent to the Ministry of the Interior, which is responsible for Civil Protection, asking why warnings about a strong and stormy bura on the Adriatic are not sent to citizens and tourists via the Early Warning and Crisis Management System (SRUUK). The ministry was also asked whether the introduction of such warnings is being considered, when they could start being sent, and whether there are any obstacles that prevent strong and stormy bura from being among the events for which citizens receive SRUUK messages.

From the response of Civil Protection it follows that Civil Protection itself doesn’t actually decide whether an SRUUK message will be sent due to a severe weather issue. They explained that the sending of SRUUK messages is regulated by the Ordinance on the procedure for early warning of the population.

warnings for severe weather events

“The early warning of the population is the provision of timely and useful information on the basis of which the competent institutions mobilise communities and individuals exposed to dangers to take measures to avoid or reduce risks and to carry out timely preparations for an effective response to threats,” they replied.

Information for early warning is collected by institutions responsible for meteorology, hydrology and flood defence, fire protection, seismology, ionising radiation, public health and geology. Operators of facilities with hazardous substances and hydro-accumulations, inspection services and scientific institutions also participate in the system. These institutions use their websites, social media channels, the traditional media and other methods as the basic channels for warnings so that the information can reach citizens as quickly as possible. Data on immediate danger are also forwarded to the Civil Protection Directorate.

who can actually issue a sruuk message urgently?

The Ordinance defines the persons who can decide to initiate the procedure for sending an SRUUK message, depending on the type of danger. In the case of floods, the decision is made by the chief flood defence manager or a person authorised by him, and in the case of large-scale fires by the chief fire commander or an authorised person.

For natural disasters and severe weather warnings, which include dangerous weather phenomena such as a strong and stormy bura, the decision is made by the director of the Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service (DHMZ) or a person authorised by him. In the case of a threat from military means, the decision is made in accordance with the Defence Act, while in the case of an immediate terrorist threat or other security reasons of a larger scale the decision is made by the chief police director or a person authorised by him.

There is also the possibility of activating the system due to an extraordinary event in the area of a particular county, city or municipality. In that case, a request with the text of the message can be submitted to the competent county 112 centre by the head of the civil protection headquarters of the local or regional self-government unit affected by the event, or a person authorised by him.

Civil Protection therefore emphasises that SRUUK is not an institution that assesses whether citizens should be warned, but a technical system by which the decision of the competent body is transmitted to people in the threatened area. “From all of the above it is clear that SRUUK is only an information tool by which early warning messages are sent to all mobile devices located in the area that the decision-maker has designated as threatened,” they state.

After receiving the decision, the Civil Protection Directorate enters the message composed by the decision-maker and sends it via mobile operators to users in the designated area.

World.title: Temperature Records Broken in Three Croatian Cities
World.content:
August the 14th, 2026 – Temperature records have been well and truly broken in three Croatian cities as the summer heat causes an array of issues nationwide.

Index reports that on the 12th of August, the City of Split recorded the highest air temperature since official records began. At the Split-Marjan measuring station at 14:00, the temperature reached a staggering 39.7 degrees Celsius.

According to official DHMZ data, this officially breaks the previous record of 39.5 degrees measured on the 30th of June this year. It still hasn’t broken the record measured back in 2017 at the Split-Kaštela meteorological station, which still stands at a horrendous 42.2 degrees Celsius.

HRT meteorologist Zoran Vakula reported that the record was also broken on the same day in Senj. 39.8°C was measured, breaking the 2015 record of 39.7°C. On the same date at 12:00 in Dubrovnik, 39.1°C was measured, breaking the 2025 record of 38.6°C.

World.title: Croatian MP Josip Dabro Pushes Harsh Measures Against Illegal Migrants
World.content:
August the 14th, 2026 – Croatian MP Josip Dabro has pushed harsh measures against illegal migrants, stating that “you can’t talk with evil, you need to shoot at evil”.

Index reports that the former DP minister and MP Josip Dabro reacted clearly and sharply to the case of a Pakistani man who imprisoned and raped a Nepalese citizen in a house near Zagreb, stating that Croatia must act significantly more harshly toward illegal migrants who commit criminal offences.

“there’s no talking with evil, you have to shoot at evil”

In a statement titled “The principle of state prevention toward illegal migrants: There is no talking with evil, you have to shoot at evil!”, he called for stricter border protection, including the use of force, and the possibility of temporarily suspending the right to seek asylum.

Dabro referred to the case of Mohamad Sh., whom he claims has been moving for years throughout Croatia and other European countries, repeatedly committing extremely serious crimes, and after police and court proceedings again seeks asylum in order to avoid deportation. He believes this case demonstrates the powerlessness of European states in dealing with people who abuse the asylum system. “What we are witnessing in this case is a public demonstration of the powerlessness and paralysis of state orders, and at the same time an invitation to everyone in the world to come and calmly, with impunity, fulfil their most perverse urges and desires,” Dabro said.

sharp criticism of lax approach by other countries

Dabro claims that the way European countries handle such cases sends the wrong message to potential perpetrators.

“Come, do whatever you want, no one can do anything to you, and on top of that you will have free accommodation, food, pocket money for condoms, possibly knives or even firearms,” he wrote, describing the message which, in his opinion, the existing system sends.

He also criticised political debates about human rights, the European legal order and the possible deployment of the army on the borders. As a positive example he highlighted the policy of US President Donald Trump, whom he claims shows how a responsible state should behave. Dabro also linked the case to earlier attacks on police officers, beatings, murders and mass brawls in Zagreb and other European cities. He claims that because of this “increasingly serious insecurity is becoming a legal European acquis”.

he advocates the use of force at the border

Dabro then set out a series of measures he considers necessary. He stated that “there is no mercy or concessions toward evil” and that nothing that is illegal must subsequently become legal. The security of the population, he believes, must primarily be defended at the state borders.

“The security of one’s own people is primarily defended at the borders, by all means and by shooting if and when necessary,” Dabro wrote. He also claims that international norms must not limit the state if it assesses that national security is threatened. In his view, in the event of a conflict between international rules and national security, such norms should be suspended. “No international norm can legally suspend the sovereign and exclusive right of the state to protect its national security by all available means,” he stated.

suspending the right to asylum

Dabro believes the state must act immediately and without, as he puts it, “false legal labyrinths”, and publicly promote such a policy in order to deter people who intend to cross the border illegally and commit criminal offences. He also called on those who oppose this approach to personally take care of illegal migrants.

“All those who have a moral objection to such state policies, instead of rhetorical one-upmanship – take in the illegal migrants, take them home, feed and care for them, share your security, prosperity and home with them, stop sharing other people’s,” he wrote. As examples of the messages the state should, in his opinion, send, he cited a case in which security forces would kill an illegal migrant during a violent attempt to cross the border, the expulsion of a perpetrator of sexual violence after a police intervention, and the temporary suspension of the right of illegal migrants to submit asylum applications.

Dabro believes such messages can have a stronger deterrent effect than increasing the number of security force members at the border, but only if the state shows it is prepared to implement them. “Whoever plans to enter Croatia illegally and cause disorder in the country must know that persecution or death awaits him, not protection and super-rights,” he said. “Let us be a nation, not a humanitarian refuge for the world’s evil,” Dabro concluded.

World.title: Croatian Tourism Campaign Starring John Malkovich Still Generating Huge Numbers
World.content:
August the 14th, 2026 – The latest and by far most celebrated Croatian tourism campaign starring the one and only John Malkovich is still generating huge numbers worldwide.

The new promotional video of the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ), “Croatia – I Hear It’s Beautiful”, starring world-famous actor John Malkovich, has achieved significant international resonance and attracted the attention of both the public and industry experts across numerous source markets.

Net.hr reports that in less than two months since its release, the main six-minute video published on YouTube and its shorter teaser version published on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok of the Croatian National Tourist Board together recorded a total of 17.3 million views, HTZ reported.

On YouTube, where the main six-minute video was published, more than 81,000 shares, more than 2,100 comments and over six million views were recorded, with the greatest interest shown by viewers from the USA, Poland, Italy, Germany, Hungary and others. The shorter version (teaser) also achieved strong audience engagement: it was shared more than 2,000 times on Facebook, more than 17,000 times on Instagram and 1,500 times on TikTok.

In addition to the reach and engagement on social media, the audience reactions to the content of the video itself are of particular value. It should be noted that a large number of positive reactions, apart from the domestic market, also came from the global audience that views the video outside the Croatian national and emotional context. For example, the response on Reddit is interesting, where the video sparked a spontaneous discussion among foreign users, with a series of positive comments highlighting its originality and humour.

Strong audience interest is also evidenced by the large number of independent reviews and reactions to the promotional video that users themselves published on YouTube. Some of these contents attracted tens of thousands of views. In them, the audience comments on and analyses the creative concept, script, humour, performance and the way Croatia is presented, which shows that the promotional video attracted attention and stimulated interest and conversation beyond the official channels of the Croatian National Tourist Board.

The international visibility of the video is additionally confirmed by more than 260 media publications on 15 source markets. These appeared in leading news media, including Kleine Zeitung, oe24, Kurier, T-Online, RTL, NU.nl, Corriere della Sera, Gazeta, WP.pl, France 24, POP TV, Delo, Dnevnik.si and Pravda, as well as in specialised B2B media such as The Drum, Travel Weekly, Travel Market Report, Media Marketing, About Travel and TTG, and lifestyle media such as Falstaff, Stern, Panorama, HelloMagyar, Roadster and Travel Squire

World.title: Hajduk Seal Conference League Play-Off Spot with Dominant 4-0 Win Against Žalgiris
World.content:
Hajduk took on Žalgiris at Poljud in the return leg of the third qualifying round for the Conference League. The Split side easily defended a 5-2 advantage secured in Lithuania seven days ago, winning 4-0 with a 9-2 aggregate. They will face Raków from Poland in the Conference League play-off round next week.

Lineups

Hajduk: Silić – Acapandie, Marešić, Raci, Melnjak – del Moral, Pajaziti – Šutalo, Dalisson, Šoticek – Livaja

Žalgiris: Sarkauskas – Šešplaukis, Lupano, Bosančić, Franke – Kendysh, Capan – Golubickas, Bilenkyi, Teixeira – Petković



Match report

The match got underway in Split at 9 pm.

The match got underway in Split, and Hajduk should have taken an early lead. In the 4th minute, Šotiček played Livaja through in the Žalgiris penalty area, leaving the Hajduk captain with only the goalkeeper to beat. Livaja struck it hard, but the ball flew over the bar — had it gone in, the goal would likely have been checked for a possible offside.

Just a minute later, Dalisson also went close, shooting from around 10 meters out, only for the Žalgiris goalkeeper to make the save. Melnjak then tested the visitors in the 11th minute, firing an effort that flew just wide of the post.

Hajduk continued to dominate, though by the 15th minute the scoreline remained unchanged from kick-off. In the 21st minute, Šotiček had a go from around twenty meters out, but his effort drifted past the goal.

In the 25th minute, Šutalo whipped in a cross from the right for Melnjak, though Kendysh got there first and headed it behind for a corner. Moments later, Dalisson produced a smart piece of defending to snuff out a Žalgiris counter-attack, carrying the ball forward some 20 meters himself before attempting to slip in a teammate — the pass was poorly executed, however, and the promising move broke down.

The game then went through a quieter spell without any major incident, and Hajduk’s resulting corners in the 28th minute failed to trouble the visitors.

In the 33rd minute, Raci tried his luck from distance, but his low effort was comfortably saved by the away goalkeeper. With 10 minutes left until the break, the half had so far been played out under Hajduk’s dominance: the hosts had squandered two big chances, held a 8-1 advantage in shots, led 4-1 on corners and enjoyed 68% of possession to the visitors’ 32%.

In the 38th minute, Franke sent in an awkward ball from the left flank, but no one managed to divert it goalwards. Marešić then blocked Bilenkyi’s follow-up attempt behind for a corner.

In the 41st minute, Šutalo earned a round of applause from the Poljud crowd. Livaja played a ball into space and the young Croatia international surged forward at the two Žalgiris defenders, who managed to stop him after he attempted to dribble past them twice. Hajduk’s right winger refused to give up, however, and won a foul and a free kick from the resulting phase of play. Nothing came of the set piece itself, though.



Hajduk dominated the first hald, but the score is 0-0 at half-time.

Hajduk finally broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute. Šutalo, excellent again, collected a long ball out on the right, drifted slightly infield, and picked out the run of Melnjak with a superb pass. Melnjak made no mistake from close range, tucking it away to make it 1-0!

In the 60th minute, Huram came on for Šotiček. In the 65th minute, Hajduk almost doubled their lead. Šutalo played it through to Livaja, who squared the ball in from the right into the box, where Melnjak was left completely unmarked to head it, but he sent his effort over the bar.

Dalisson then tried his luck from distance in the 66th minute, though his shot was off target. A minute later, Šutalo had a go himself from 18 meters out, but also failed to hit the target. In the 68th minute, Hajduk made a triple change, with Šego, Brruti and Sigur coming on to replace Livaja, Dalisson and Pajaziti.

Hajduk doubled their advantage in the 69th minute. Acapandie crossed from the right for Šego, whose effort cannoned off an opponent’s head, with the loose ball falling kindly for 17-year-old Huram. The teenager reacted brilliantly, turning smartly to fire home and make it 2-0.



In the 75th minute, Bamba came on for Šutalo and made it 3-0 five minutes later. Three minutes after that, Šego made it 4-0, which was the final result.

With this 9-2 aggregate, Hajduk moves on to the Conference League play-offs. The first leg will be played on August 20th at Poljud, with the return leg scheduled for August 27th.

World.title: Croatian Tourism Minister Says Last Minute Bookings are Saving August
World.content:
August the 13th, 2026 – The Croatian tourism minister has stated that last minute bookings are saving August, with more and more people paying closer attention to value for money before making reservations.

Croatian tourism is once again confirming its strength this year, and the results achieved show that we are on the right track, said Tonči Glavina, Minister of Tourism and Sport. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that the month of July’s tourism results were better than expected, and indications suggest that the second half of the summer could follow the same pattern.

According to data from the eVisitor system, which records tourist traffic in commercial and non-commercial facilities as well as nautical charters (eCrew system), Croatia recorded 12.4 million arrivals and 59.1 million overnight stays from January to the end of July. Compared with the same period last year, this represents growth of 1 percent in both arrivals and overnight stays.

Of that total, 56.1 million overnight stays were recorded on the Adriatic (up 0.5 percent year-on-year), while the continent, including the city of Zagreb, recorded more than 3 million overnight stays (up 1 percent).

july was fantastic for croatia

eVisitor data also shows that in July this year, Croatia recorded 4.7 million arrivals and 29.6 million overnight stays, which is an increase of 2.5 percent in arrivals and 1 percent in overnight stays compared with July last year. In the seventh month the most guests came from the markets of Germany, Slovenia, Croatia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary and others. By counties, the most tourists were counted in Istria, Split-Dalmatia County and Kvarner, while the most visited destinations were Rovinj, Vir, Poreč, Medulin and Dubrovnik.

“We are satisfied with the tourism results achieved in the first seven months of this year, and especially with the fact that in July we recorded the best result of the last two years. This confirms that Croatian tourism continues to maintain its competitiveness and resilience and that, despite changes in the market, we are succeeding in maintaining positive trends. We are particularly pleased that good results are also being recorded in financial indicators.

In July the value of fiscalised invoices rose by 18 percent, while the number of issued invoices was 8 percent higher than in the same month last year. Growth is also being recorded in road, air and maritime traffic, and all these results confirm that we have responded well to market circumstances – both through quality promotion of Croatia and through timely adaptation of the offer. I thank the entire tourism sector for the effort invested, and especially accommodation providers who responded to our appeals and, with their promotional offers, additionally contributed to the competitiveness of our offer.

Ahead of us is still a good part of August, after which we will make a complete overview of this main part of the tourist year. Croatian tourism is once again confirming its strength this year, and the results achieved show that we are on the right track and that together we are successfully responding to changes and challenges,” said Tonči Glavina, Minister of Tourism and Sport.

When Croatia’s tourism results are broken down by counties, in the first seven months the most overnight stays were recorded in Istria (16.7 million), Split-Dalmatia County (11.1 million) and Kvarner (9.7 million), while by destinations the leaders were Dubrovnik, Rovinj, Poreč, Split and Umag.

last minute to the rescue

“The course and results of the tourist year so far show that Croatia still has a very strong position on the global tourism market, despite all the demanding circumstances. What we particularly read from this year’s tourist movements is a change in the way guests make decisions about their trips. Last-minute bookings play an important role, and when choosing a destination, the best value for money is increasingly sought, along with safety and easy accessibility. In this context Croatia has a series of advantages – from proximity to our most important source markets and good transport connections to the diversity of the offer that enables different types of holidays.

Given the considerable number of promotional last-minute arrangement prices in August, the tourism sector believes that the August figures will also be good.

The results achieved therefore give us additional wind in our sails for the continuation of the tourist year, all the more so because the Ferragosto period is ahead of us, traditionally very important for travel by Italian guests. In addition to the main summer months, we are also recording excellent advance bookings for the shoulder season, for which promotional activities begin in mid-August, especially on the Polish and UK markets,” said Kristjan Staničić, director of the Croatian National Tourist Board.

Looking at markets, during the first seven months the most overnight stays were recorded by guests from Germany (10.3 million), Croatia (7.6 million), Slovenia (6.7 million), Austria (4.3 million), Poland (3.9 million), the Czech Republic (3 million), the UK (2.2 million), Hungary (2.1 million) and others.

Given the considerable number of promotional last-minute arrangement prices in August, the tourism sector believes that the August figures will also be good, at least at last year’s level.

59.1 million overnight stays were recorded over the first seven months of this year

Interesting trends can also be seen on individual markets. Thus eVisitor figures show that Croatian tourism in July and during the first seven months of 2026 recorded significant growth in tourist traffic from the Czech, Hungarian and Italian markets.

The most pronounced positive shift was recorded on the Czech market. Compared with July last year, the number of arrivals of Czech tourists rose by 12 percent, while the number of their overnight stays was higher by seven percent. In the period from January to the end of July growth of five percent was recorded in both arrivals and overnight stays compared with the same period last year. The Hungarian market is also a reason for satisfaction. During July the number of arrivals of Hungarian tourists increased by eight percent, while the number of overnight stays rose by seven percent.

In the first seven months of the year growth of seven percent was recorded in both arrivals and overnight stays compared with last year. Hungarian guests stayed most on Kvarner, in Istria and Zadar County. The Italian market, which had stagnated in recent years, is also recovering. In the period from January to July the number of arrivals and overnight stays of Italian guests increased by two percent compared with the same period last year, while in July a one-percent growth in arrivals was recorded.

World.title: Croats are Travelling Less and Taking Less Annual Leave This Summer
World.content:
August the 13th, 2026 – Croats appear to be travelling less and taking less annual leave this summer, with the latest research into these habits showing a marked change.

Almost every third person in Croatia is staying at their usual place of residence this summer, primarily due to a lack of financial resources, according to a survey conducted by Alma Career Croatia. Poslovni reports that the results of the latest survey on annual leave, carried out by Alma Career Croatia, an international company best known for the MojPosao/MyJob portal, show that Croatian employees are planning their holidays a little more cautiously this summer.

According to this latest survey, Croatian workers enjoy an average of 25 days of annual leave, and summer is the period when most employees use the largest part of their free days. However, this year’s results show that habits are slowly changing.

shorter summer breaks

Compared with 2025, the number of workers who plan to use fewer days of annual leave during the summer is rising, as is the number of those who aren’t planning on taking any trips at all this year.

The share of employees who plan to use a maximum of seven days of annual leave has increased from 15% in 2025 to 21% in 2026. On the other hand, the share of those planning to rest for 21 days or longer has almost halved (7% last year, 3% this year). The most common choice remains a holiday lasting 8 to 10 days, planned by 37% of respondents. This is followed by those who will rest between 11 and 15 days (29%), while 10% of employees plan annual leave lasting between 15 and 20 days.

The issue with summer that is becoming increasingly problematic is the fact that the weather is becoming so insufferably hot that sitting under the air conditioner is the only choice for a growing number of people. Most can do that at work or at home.

the croatian coast still dominates for most croats, as opposed to heading somewhere abroad

When it comes to destination, Croatia remains the first choice.

More than half of the survey participants (56%) plan to spend their summer holiday within the country, which is only slightly less than last year, when the figure was 58%. There are also somewhat fewer people planning a trip abroad this summer. Their share has fallen from 21% in 2025 to 17% this year.

However, the biggest change is visible among those who do not plan to travel at all. Their share has risen in one year from 27% to 32%, meaning that almost every third respondent will not go on a summer holiday this year. Finances are most often behind such a decision. Among respondents who will not travel, as many as 60% cite lack of financial resources as the main reason, compared with 56% last year.

One to two weeks on the Adriatic; shorter or longer holidays abroad

There are also differences in the length of holidays depending on whether respondents holiday in Croatia or travel abroad. Those who holiday somewhere else within Croatia most often choose a classic break of one to two weeks. As many as 78% of them plan to rest between 8 and 15 days.

People who travel abroad more often choose either very short or significantly longer trips. Thus, 21% of respondents travelling outside Croatia plan a holiday of seven days or less, while among those staying in Croatia the figure is 10%. At the other end of the spectrum, 7% of travellers abroad plan a holiday longer than three weeks, while among those holidaying in Croatia only 2% plan such a break.

World.title: Popular Lebanese restaurant Al Beiruti to open in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Al Beiruti, a popular Lebanese restaurant, is set to build its first Iraqi branch in Iraq Mall in Baghdad, adding another significant regional dining name to the capital’s growing restaurant scene.

The Baghdad inauguration will be the next chapter of Al Beiruti’s regional development, after previous launches in Jordan and Qatar, as well as its established presence in the UAE.

The restaurant announced that its Iraq Mall restaurant is about to open, with a local franchise arrangement handling the expansion.

Al Beiruti has become a renowned location for Lebanese food in the Middle East, providing both classic dishes and a more modern restaurant experience.

The menu includes Lebanese favorites, including manakish, fattoush, hummus, baba ghanouj, and grilled halloumi, as well as shawarma, wraps, and mixed grills. Larger meals include steak, chicken escalope, and grilled salmon.

Al Beiruti joins a growing number of international and regional food and beverage companies in Baghdad, as new malls and commercial expansions change the city’s retail and entertainment markets.

Iraq Mall has emerged as a focal point of that expansion, drawing new restaurants, boutiques, and entertainment ideas as consumer spending and private-sector investment continue to rise in the capital.

World.title: Baghdad and Erbil agree on unified digital customs system across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Baghdad and Erbil have agreed to fully adopt the digital ASYCUDA customs system across border crossings, with non-oil border earnings shared equally by the federal and Kurdistan regional governments.

The deal is a significant step toward standardizing customs processes across Iraq and addressing long-standing disagreements over border revenues and claimed import quantities.

ASYCUDA, designed by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), digitizes customs declarations, payments, and clearing processes, allowing authorities to better monitor products entering the nation and the income they earn.

Linking customs operations to Iraq’s banking and electronic payment systems may help limit the potential for underreporting, revenue leakage, and corruption at border crossings.

The deal comes as Iraq’s Finance Ministry and Central Bank work to digitize customs, payments, and government financial data in collaboration with UNCTAD.

A combined computerized customs system for Baghdad and Erbil might give more accurate revenue data while resolving one of the two governments’ ongoing financial issues.

The change is also significant for Iraq’s overall economy.

More open and uniform customs processes might facilitate cross-border commerce, boost governmental revenues, and enhance the business climate as Iraq pursues more foreign investment and closer integration with international markets.

World.title: Iraq’s Chief Justice Faiq Zidan meets Syrian President Al-Sharaa in Damascus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Thursday, marking another high-level Iraqi outreach to a neighboring Arab state as Baghdad seeks to bolster regional relations under rising security problems.

Al-Sharaa welcomed Zidan and an Iraqi delegation to the People’s Palace, which also included Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Justice Minister Mazhar al-Wais.

According to the Syrian president, the talks focused on extending judicial and legal cooperation between Iraq and Syria, as well as resolving mutual concerns.

The visit also resulted in more practical conversations among the two nations’ judicial officials. Iraqi and Syrian authorities agreed to set up joint judicial committees to continue working on cases involving Syrian prisoners and other cross-border legal issues.

Zidan’s visit is crucial as he is one of the most prominent persons in Iraq’s state institutions, and it coincides with Baghdad’s increased diplomatic, security, and judicial interaction with its neighbors.

The Damascus meetings come after a separate Iraqi security group visited Riyadh, where senior military official Abdul Amir al-Shammari met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman.

Zidan had also just visited Ankara as part of a larger Iraqi effort to build ties with Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Turkey.

That approach has become more urgent in light of the regional escalation involving Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

In late July, the United States and Saudi Arabia conducted synchronized attacks against locations used by Iran-aligned organizations in Iraq, after Riyadh accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones against Saudi energy infrastructure.

The incident put Baghdad under strong pressure to prevent armed organizations from exploiting Iraqi territory to launch assaults on neighboring nations and also highlighted the potential that militia activity may harm Iraq’s improved ties with Arab governments.

Against this setting, Zidan’s encounter with Al-Sharaa is significant beyond regular court cooperation.

Iraq and Syria share a long border and confront shared concerns such as terrorism, organized crime, prisoners, and cross-border security. Baghdad also has a strategic interest in preserving stable ties with Damascus, as Iraq strives to boost regional connections and prevent unrest from spilling over its borders.

Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration sees recent diplomatic efforts as part of a larger effort to strengthen Iraq’s ties with its neighbors while keeping the nation out of the developing conflict between Iran and its regional adversaries.

Baghdad has increasingly emphasized that choices on security, armament, and relations with neighboring governments must be made by Iraqi official authorities rather than armed groupings.

The travels to Damascus and Riyadh therefore convey an essential message: although Iran-aligned militias have exacerbated tensions between Iraq and certain of its neighbors, Iraqi official institutions are working directly with those nations to restore cooperation and avoid further escalation.

Strengthening judicial, diplomatic, and security ties with Syria, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey might serve as an essential regional buffer for Iraq as it seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, control armed groups, and avoid being drawn further into the region’s crises.

World.title: Iraq’s Al-Shammari visits Riyadh to meet Saudi Defense Minister
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A top Iraqi security team has traveled to Riyadh for meetings with Saudi Arabia’s leadership, as Baghdad and the Kingdom work to improve security and military cooperation after weeks of heightened tensions in Iraq involving Iran-backed militias.

First Lieutenant General Abdul Amir Al-Shammari, director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman on Thursday to discuss military cooperation, regional developments, and increased coordination between the two nations.

According to reports from the visit, the conversations included cross-border drone concerns, air defense, and intelligence collaboration.

The conference is especially significant in light of the combined US-Saudi attacks on Iran-linked militia locations in Iraq on July 29.

Washington and Riyadh said the operation targeted Iran-backed terrorists’ weapons and logistical facilities in response to a series of drone assaults on Saudi oil installations that they said originated in Iraqi territory.

The strikes drastically escalated tensions between Baghdad and Riyadh, highlighting the Iraqi government’s problems in preventing armed groups from exploiting its territory to target neighboring nations.

Thursday’s visit indicates that both parties are now attempting to move beyond that conflict via direct military and intelligence collaboration.

Prince Khalid underlined Saudi Arabia’s commitment to Iraq’s security, stability, and economic growth, identifying it as an essential neighbor with whom the Kingdom has strong political and social relations.

The meetings in Riyadh follow Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali al-Humaidan’s visit to Baghdad last week, during which he met with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and reiterated an offer for the Iraqi leader to visit Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad’s security cooperation with Riyadh has grown more vital as the government seeks to prevent Iran-backed militias from drawing Iraq into a larger regional conflict.

Al-Zaidi has frequently said that Iraqi soil should not be used to attack other nations and has stepped up efforts for weaponry to be put solely under state control.

The most recent Iraqi trip to Riyadh symbolizes more than just normal defense diplomacy. It is part of a joint effort by Baghdad and Saudi Arabia to restore security trust after the July escalation and prevent militia activities from dragging the two neighboring nations into conflict.

World.title: Rare blind fish found in underground river in Iraq’s Anbar desert
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security and environmental teams have discovered a fascinating underground water system deep under the dry Anbar desert, where rare eyeless fish thrive in total darkness.

The location is in the Al-Khasfa region near Haditha, and crews traveled through a remote desert cave and sinkhole system to access running groundwater hundreds of meters under the surface.

The expedition’s footage shows little, pale fish moving in the subterranean water in the lack of sunshine.

The fish have evolved to live in darkness by losing their eyes and pigmentation, giving them a characteristic white-to-pink look.

The crew traveled more than 500 meters into the cave system despite challenging terrain and low oxygen levels.

The difference between above- and underground has piqued interest: underneath what seems to be an isolated and very arid stretch of western Iraqi desert, there is flowing freshwater and a specialized ecology.

Initial investigations have also suggested a link between the subterranean water system and the Euphrates basin, with the watercourse possibly running for a long distance under the desert.

However, environmental experts have highlighted that the blind fish themselves are not a novel finding.

Qais Najeh, the chairman of the Anbar Environment Directorate, stated that experts first confirmed the occurrence of eyeless fish in Al-Khasfa in 2010.

Similar fish have also been discovered in subterranean water near the Sheik Hadid mausoleum in Haditha district.

According to experts, the fish may grow to be roughly 49 millimeters long and survive in rather steady groundwater temperatures ranging from 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

Their lack of vision and pigmentation are adaptations to generations of living in perpetually dark subterranean habitats.

The recent mission is nonetheless noteworthy because it has refocused attention on one of Iraq’s least-known natural ecosystems, perhaps allowing scientists to better research the subterranean water network, its geology, and the creatures that rely on it.

The fish’s severely limited environment renders it vulnerable.

Changes in groundwater levels, pollution, or human intervention might endanger a population that has acclimated to highly particular subsurface circumstances.

The Al-Khasfa location offers a unique dimension to Anbar, a region best known for its wide western desert and the Euphrates.

Hidden under that terrain lies an environment few Iraqis have ever seen: flowing subterranean water that feeds fish who have evolved to survive their entire lives without sunshine.

World.title: Israel reopens once-closed West Bank settlement
World.content:
GANIM – Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government’s policy of rapid settlement expansion.

The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim’s new and only street, where future residents and their families — who had come to help with the move — smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.

“A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We’re arriving now,” new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.

In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.

Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government’s policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.

“I’m happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly,” he said.

Berkovitch’s mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.

“Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.

Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan in 2005.

The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.

Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities — Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.

In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.

About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.

“The era of evacuation is over — from here, we only build,” Dagan said.

In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim’s construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.

On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

World.title: Carrick urges Man Utd to push for more signings to boost title bid
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick has urged Manchester United to splash the cash to keep pace with their Premier League title rivals.

United have spent around £85 million ($114 million) on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow since the end of last season.

But that outlay pales in comparison to some of United’s fellow title contenders, with Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea all paying huge fees for high-profile signings.

Carrick knows United need more quality and depth if they are to challenge for a first English title since 2013, while also competing in the Champions League.

Remarkably, United have never spent more than £89.5 million on a single player — the fee paid for Paul Pogba in 2016.

And ahead of his first season as permanent United boss after a successful interim spell last term, Carrick called on the club’s hierarchy to push for more new recruits.

“I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

“We’re delighted with that. We always want to improve. We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that. That never stops.”

Carrick led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League after he replaced the sacked Ruben Amorim.

But with United so far spending less than promoted sides Coventry and Ipswich, some fans are becoming restless as their Premier League opener at Hull on August 22 looms into view.

“Money’s money, I get that. It’s still about the football, and that’s where the competition lies,” Carrick said.

“Certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever. For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing and push everything and every boundary that we can to be able to win again.”

Asked why United were not spending on the level of other clubs, Carrick added: “To be honest, I haven’t got the answers for that. We’re working with pushing everything that we can to make the best of it.”

Having spent last season on loan with Barcelona, Marcus Rashford is back at United this week after returning from the World Cup.

Barcelona declined their option to buy the 28-year-old England forward and questions remain over his United future.

“He’s our player, and he’s a good player and he gives us something a little bit different in the group,” he said.

“Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect it’s quite exciting.”

Several United players have backed the team to dethrone Arsenal as champions and the understated Carrick wouldn’t rule out a title push.

“We’ve definitely got the potential to achieve something really special,” he said.

“I’m not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that, but I can’t give you a definite answer on that.

“It’s certainly what we’re pushing to do because we have to, because that’s the club we are.”

World.title: Leicester’s Thai owners put troubled club up for sale: reports
World.content:
London – Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

World.title: ‘Congress responsible for Partition’: CM Yogi says India would be different if Modi were PM in 1947
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister

has accused the Congress of being responsible for India's Partition and the violence that followed, arguing that the country's history could have been different under leaders such as Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel or Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Speaking at an event in Lucknow marking Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, CM Yogi said the Congress had failed the country by prioritising political power and alleged that the consequences of Partition continue to affect India.

âHad Narendra Modi been the Prime Minister of India at the time of Independence, nobody would have been able to damage India in the slightest,â he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.

He also invoked Patel, saying that a leader of his stature would not have allowed India to be divided.

âIf a person like Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were the Prime Minister at that time, nobody would have been able to disintegrate India ... The country had to pay a heavy price for the cowardice of these Congress members -- a character you all witnessed during the CAA protests,â he added.

Adityanath alleged that areas including Sindh, Punjab and Bengal were handed over to Pakistan despite what he described as their Hindu and regional demographic character.





âBengal was Bengali-dominated. All Hindu villages were forcibly given to Bangladesh. This shameful act was committed by the Congress, which was extra-restless for power, and on whom the country had reposed its trust. It repaid that trust with betrayal,â he said.

The chief minister also criticised the Congress over its response to attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh. He alleged that the party remained silent because it was concerned about losing electoral support.

âThey feared that reacting to the events in Bangladesh might cause their vote bank here to drift away. To them, the murder of Dalit Hindus holds no significance; what matters is their own vote bank,â he said.

Adityanath further argued that internal divisions based on caste, region and language had historically weakened India and created opportunities for outside forces.

âWhen such infighting exists, then conspiracy easily creeps in,â he said.

He said the consequences of Partition could still be seen in the form of terrorism, Naxalism, Maoism and extremism. He also questioned the Congress's claims about its role in India's freedom struggle and accused the party of presenting itself as indispensable to the creation of modern India.

âThis also draws our attention to the silence we have all maintained regarding that pre-1947 conspiracy. Yet, even today, these people move before society, acting as if they were the ones who created India, and that without them, India would not have come into existence.

It is a truly strange situation,â he said, describing Partition as the âdarkest chapter of humanity.â

Turning to what he described as the Congress's political legacy, Adityanath said institutions across the country had been named after one political family.

âEvery institution in the country came to bear the name of that very clan. Every single institution was named after that clan, and we all stood by silently, merely watching.

What are they doing even today? What are their actions like now?â he said.

The

also defended the

and attacked the Congress's opposition to it.

âThere was no justification for opposing the act. The act contained a provision regarding Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Bangladesh -- territories that were once part of undivided India and share a heritage spanning thousands of years. It stipulated that if a Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Buddhist, Parsi, or Christian from these countries had been forced to leave and had sought refuge in India for five years, they would be granted Indian citizenship,â he said.

He argued that the legislation did not provide for taking away land or property from Muslims or political parties, and accused opponents of using the issue to provoke protests.

âNowhere did it say that we would seize land belonging to Muslims, the Congress, or the Samajwadi Party. There was no such provision in the Act. Yet, attempts were made to incite agitation across the country,â he said.

World.title: 'First time we did something like this': Former women Naxalites share their Raipur ramp-walk experience
World.content:
NEW DELHI: For nine women from Chhattisgarh's Naxal-affected Bastar region, the stage in Raipur offered a strikingly different kind of experience. Once part of an armed insurgency, they recently walked the ramp in handloom outfits at a National Handloom Day event, as part of efforts to help surrendered Naxalites rebuild their lives.

The women, all from Sukma, took part in a Swadeshi fashion show organised as part of rehabilitation efforts for former Naxalites.

Sukma SP Mayank Gurjar said the event also gave them an opportunity to promote Swadeshi products.

For some of the women, the experience was unlike anything they had done before. One former Naxalite, who had worked with the Pamed Area Committee, said she surrendered in 2026 and travelled to Raipur for six days of training before taking part in the programme.

"I used to work in the Pamed Area Committee. I surrendered in 2026. We went to Raipur recently. There, we were trained by people who had come from Bombay...prominent ministers also came. The training was of six days...it was the first time we did something like that...we enjoyed it," the former Naxalite told news agency ANI.

Another participant, Poonam Devi, said her journey with the Naxalite movement had begun in November 2007.





She surrendered on July 12, 2025, bringing that chapter of her life to an end.

"I surrendered on July 12, 2025. I liked the program...we were trained for it...I joined the Naxals in November 2007 and left in 2025," she said.

According to Gurjar, the women's participation reflects the opportunities being offered under the rehabilitation policies of the Central and Chhattisgarh governments to those who surrender and choose to return to mainstream society.

"As you all know, through the rehabilitation policy of the Government of India and the Chhattisgarh Government, various benefits and advantages are being provided to surrendered Naxalites. In that context, on National Handloom Day, nine surrendered women who had surrendered in Sukma participated in a Swadeshi fashion show," he said.

The nine women had held different positions within the Naxalite organisation.

Some were associated with the Pamed Area Committee, while others had served as gunners for senior Naxalite commanders in Battalion Number 1. One had worked as a school teacher within the organisation, according to the SP.

"Among the nine surrendered women, some were working in the Pamed Area Committee. Some worked as gunners for major Naxalite commanders in Battalion Number 1. One of the surrendered women Naxalites was working as a teacher in a school," Gurjar said.

Their past also included handling weapons. Gurjar said one of the women had carried an INSAS rifle and that the participants had surrendered around six months earlier.

Now, instead of carrying weapons, the women are being encouraged to explore skills and opportunities that can help them build a different future.

Gurjar said their participation in the fashion show showed a change in their outlook and suggested that their confidence in the rehabilitation process was growing.

"They are now actively promoting Swadeshi products and refining their artistic skills," he said.

For women who once lived amid the forests and violence of the Naxal movement, walking a ramp in handloom clothing may appear like a small moment. But within the larger rehabilitation effort, it represents something much more significant, a visible step away from an armed past and towards an ordinary life.

World.title: 'Serious doubts on intent': Congress attacks Centre over caste census format; cites Telangana model
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Friday questioned the Centre's approach to caste enumeration in the upcoming Census, saying the decision not to provide a pre-prepared list of castes for respondents to choose from raised âserious doubts on intentâ.

The party also alleged that political parties had not been consulted on the questionnaire.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said it was widely expected that the caste question would include a state-wise list, similar to the caste surveys conducted in Bihar and Telangana, with respondents required to tick the appropriate option.

âThis has, unfortunately, not happened, raising serious doubts on intent,â Ramesh said in a post on X.

Kharge's suggestions 'ignored'

Ramesh also shared Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's May 5, 2025 letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the caste census, saying Kharge's âvery first and fundamental suggestionâ had been ignored.

Kharge had urged the government to draw on the Telangana caste survey model while finalising the Census questionnaire and had also called for consultations with all political parties.

He had argued that caste data should not be collected merely for counting communities but should help achieve wider socio-economic objectives.





Centre notifies 40 questions

The Centre on Friday notified 40 questions to be asked during the population enumeration phase of Census 2027, including questions on caste and the place of Covid vaccination, news agency ANI reports.

A government notification said respondents would be asked whether they belonged to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and, separately, about their caste. Sources said the questionnaire is unlikely to carry a pre-prepared list of castes, with responses instead being recorded as provided by respondents.

This will be the first time caste details are being collected as part of the decennial Census.

World.title: 'Astronauts' land on road craters: Over 100 Jaipur residents stage unique protest against potholes
World.content:
A man dressed as astronauts stands in a waterlogged road crater to highlight civic issues and protest against waterlogging in the Jhotwara area, in Jaipur (PTI photo)

Residents say potholes have become 'Moon and Mars' craters

NEW DELHI: What if you could experience the Moon without leaving Jaipur? More than 100 residents of Gokulpura in the Jhotwara assembly area attempted to answer that question on Thursday by turning their neighbourhood's pothole-riddled roads into a makeshift lunar landscape.Residents of Gokulpura's wards 46 and 47 staged a two-hour protest from 10 am to noon on Pratap Circle Road, with two protesters dressed as astronauts and stepping into large, water-filled potholes.The unusual protest was aimed at highlighting the condition of roads and drainage in the area, which residents said has deteriorated after recent rains.The protesters said they have been trying for around three months to draw the attention of Jhotwara MLA and minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore, Jaipur rural MP Rao Rajendra Singh, former councillors and officials of the Jaipur Development Authority (JDA) and Jaipur Municipal Corporation (JMC).Some residents alleged that they had repeatedly failed to meet Rathore, while on some occasions his staff told them he was âbusyâ.Protester Devendra Pratap Singh said the astronaut-themed protest was meant to underline the scale of the problem.âIf potholes resemble the Moon and Mars, why spend billions on rockets when Jhotwara is already offering the full experience, complete with monsoon water features,â Singh said.He added that the protest was intended to show that the potholes left after the rains had become so large that they resembled craters on the Moon and Mars.Residents raised concerns over broken roads, poor drainage and large potholes that have worsened following the recent rains.Sources told TOI that tenders for drainage and road construction work in the constituency have already been awarded. The work is expected to begin after the monsoon ends.

World.title: BCI action, U-turn and SC rebuke: How NALSAR students' protest against CJI kicked up a row
World.content:
CJI Surya Kant rebukes BCI over NALSAR enrolment ban, says students have right to protest peacefully.

How the NALSAR row began

BCI threatens to block enrolment

BCI retracts order within hours

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Friday strongly disapproved of the Bar Council of India's now-revoked decision to stop enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law as advocates after students opposed his invitation as chief guest for the university's convocation. The Supreme Court said students had a right to protest peacefully and stayed any coercive action against NALSAR students or faculty by the BCI or state Bar Councils."If students are protesting peacefully, who is BCI to take action? It is the right of the students to protest peacefully. It is a dialogue between students and me. No one else has to step in," the CJI said.The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said the BCI's action was "absolutely uncalled for". The court posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.The controversy began after a section of NALSAR students urged the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant as chief guest for its upcoming convocation. The students had cited his reported remarks during a hearing on alleged police excesses against protesters during the July 20 march to Parliament.At least six representations were submitted to the NALSAR administration from students of different batches, with the first being submitted on July 23.The students objected to the proposed invitation and referred to remarks attributed to the CJI during the hearing.One of the representations cited his response to an offer to show videos of the alleged police action: "We are not interested in videos; we donât have time to watch." The letter also quoted him as telling counsel: "Donât waste our time, and donât waste your time".The students argued that inviting the CJI conflicted with the university's stated commitment to constitutional rights and access to justice."A convocation is meant to be a moment where the Universityâs own values, including a commitment to constitutional rights, access to justice, and reasoned engagement with grievances, are visibly reflected in the choices it makes. We feel that receiving our degrees from a dignitary whose recent public conduct, as reported, appears dismissive of serious allegations of police brutality against protesting citizens sits uncomfortably with what we have been taught to value during our time at NALSAR. "Five subsequent representations from different batches supported the concerns raised in the initial letter. Students claimed that hundreds had backed the representations, although the numbers could not be independently verified."We respect the CJIâs position. But we have been taught the Constitution and constitutional values, and we donât want to support something that goes against those values," a student who was also part of the Student Bar Council told TOI.The issue escalated on Thursday when BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra directed state Bar Councils not to enrol NALSAR's 2026 law graduates as advocates until further orders.The BCI sought a factual report from NALSAR on those who had allegedly initiated, organised or mobilised the campaign against CJI Kant's participation in the convocation.âTill further orders, no student of Nalsar University of Law, who has obtained law degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any state bar council as an advocate.âMishra said the final decision would be taken on August 19 after receiving a report from the university's vice-chancellor. He also asked NALSAR to distinguish between students who merely signed or supported representations and those who organised or coordinated the campaign or proposed an actual boycott.The BCI's initial letter also said, âA student of Law, having no regard or respect for the highest judicial office of the country, is not expected to be a responsible or sensible advocate, teacher or a judge. Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the personâs suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession. âThe council further alleged that some academic staff had been involved in "misleading, instigating and misguiding" students.âAs per some reliable sources, there exists groupism and dirty politics among some of the academic staff and they have played a very active role in misleading, instigating and misguiding the students. This is a very serious matter. The teachers, instead of involving themselves in their teaching job, are doing nasty politics in the campus. BCI, being the regulator of Legal Education cannot be a mute spectator of such a serious situation. âThe decision triggered criticism, including from Supreme Court Bar Association president Vikas Singh, who called the move arbitrary, illegal and disproportionate, although he said he did not support the students' opposition to the CJI's invitation.The BCI withdrew its initial directive later on Thursday following widespread criticism.In its revised communication, Mishra said the council had âthoroughly discussed and deliberatedâ on the earlier letter and modified its direction.He said the âvast majorityâ of NALSAR's 2026 graduating students were innocent and âwere not inclined to take part in the move of disrespectâ. However, he added that âIt has been further reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating innocent students.âThe BCI subsequently allowed the 2026 graduates to be enrolled while awaiting an inquiry report from NALSAR.On Friday, the Supreme Court's intervention effectively brought the focus back to the students' right to peacefully express their disagreement with the proposed convocation invitation.Kant said the matter represented a direct dialogue between the students and him, making clear that other institutions should not intervene in the students' peaceful protest.

World.title: SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahabadia in ‘India’s Got Latent’ case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Friday quashed all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahbadia and others in connection with insensitive remarks made against persons with disabilities on the show Indiaâs Got Latent, according to Bar and Bench.

The controversy began after Allahbadia appeared on Raina's Indiaâs Got Latent show and made remarks that were widely criticised as obscene and offensive. Multiple complaints and FIRs followed across states, with allegations including promotion of obscenity and use of indecent language.

Allahbadia approached the Supreme Court seeking consolidation of the FIRs and protection from coercive action. During the proceedings, the court strongly criticised his remarks and observed that freedom of speech did not give anyone a licence to use language that violated societal norms.

The court also granted him interim protection and allowed him to seek police security after reports of death threats.

SC warns Samay Raina over Canada remarks

The matter returned to the Supreme Court in March 2025 after Raina made comments about the case during a show in Canada.

On March 3, 2025, the Supreme Court sternly warned Raina against discussing the proceedings publicly and taking the court lightly.

âThese youngsters may think that we are outdated, but we know how to deal with them.





Don't take the court lightly," Justice Surya Kant said during the hearing.

The remarks came after Raina joked with an audience in Canada at the end of his show, saying, âThanks for paying my lawyerâs fees.â

The bench of Justices Surya Kant and N Kotiswar Singh also considered Allahbadia's request to resume his podcast, The Ranveer Show. The court allowed him to resume the podcast while stressing the need to balance morality with freedom of expression.

The court took note of Allahbadia's submission that the podcast was his only source of livelihood and that around 280 people employed by him depended on the show.

The bench also extended Allahbadia's interim protection from arrest and directed him to join the investigation in Guwahati.

SC raps Raina, Allahbadia over non-compliance

The case again came under scrutiny on July 14, 2026, when the Supreme Court came down heavily on Raina and Allahbadia for allegedly failing to comply with its earlier directions.

The court described Raina and Allahbadia as "self-styled youth icons" and expressed serious concern over their alleged non-compliance with its orders.

The Supreme Court imposed a fine of Rs 3 lakh each on Raina and the other respondents and granted them two weeks to file a compliance affidavit.

âWe have no reason to doubt that Samay Raina has taken the court for a ride. He is in brazen violation of statements/ undertakings given before this court," the court said.

The CJI also observed that the respondents appeared to believe that being outside India placed them beyond the court's jurisdiction.

âLet them suffer now. If this is not arrogance, then we have to change the Oxford dictionary also," the CJI observed.

The July proceedings marked another sharp intervention by the court in the long-running controversy, months after it had cautioned Raina against making public comments about the case.

Delhi high court receives bomb threat via email

NEW DELHI: A day before Independence Day, the Delhi High Court, Terminal 3 of Delhi airport and several government offices in the national capital received bomb threats via email on Friday.Police declared all the threats hoaxes after carrying out searches and security checks at the locations.A police source said the Delhi Cantonment SDM Office received an email at 11.18 am, followed by Terminal 3 of Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI) at 11:32 am, Jamnagar House at 11.40 am, Saket SDM Office at 11:42 am and Jhandewalan at 11:57 am. The threats were reported to the Fire Control Room.The threatening email reportedly referred to August 15 and carried the warning, âLal Qila ta nishana hove gaâ (the Red Fort will be targeted). It also claimed that those carrying out the bombing would be dressed in khaki, apparently suggesting the involvement of uniformed personnel in the alleged operation.Teams from the Delhi Police, bomb squad and fire brigade were sent to all five locations, and the threats were declared hoaxes after checks."The bomb threat appears to be fake... Everything is under control. Bomb squad and sniffer dogs are scanning the entire premises.There is no threat as of now," said joint secretary of the Delhi High Court, Advocate Kunal.Security has been heightened across the national capital ahead of Independence Day, with police personnel deployed at strategic points and additional checks being conducted at entry and exit routes.Security teams are also keeping a close watch on public places and areas expected to see increased movement ahead of August 15.

World.title: Kerala’s Congress MLA C.R. Mahesh apologises for seat belt violation
World.content:
Congress MLA C.R. Mahesh on Friday (August 14, 2026) apologised for travelling without wearing a seat belt, saying it was a violation of traffic rules and that he regretted the lapse.

In a Facebook post, the MLA from Karunagappally in Kerala, said travelling without a seat belt was against the law and admitted that such a mistake happened on his part.

“Many people violate traffic rules knowingly or unknowingly. However, elected representatives should not commit such lapses,” he said in the post.

Mr. Mahesh said he recalled that the violation occurred while he was travelling to visit the tomb of former Kerala Chief Minister Oommen Chandy at Puthuppally church ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections.

Says fines paid

He said, as far as he remembered, he had paid the fines for all such cases when he contested the election.

“If not, I will ensure that the fine is paid and take care not to repeat the mistake,” he said.

Mr. Mahesh said he was issuing the statement after the incident was reported by the visual media.

“I apologise for the incident and thank the media for pointing out the mistake,” the MLA added.

World.title: How poets and artistes kept alive the spirit of freedom
World.content:
In a land as vast and diverse as pre-Independence India, and long before the telecommunication revolution, the flame of patriotism was lit by the written, spoken and sung word. Poets used their pens as weapons of resistance and inspired people to put the Nation before self. It was through these literary works that the stories of courage and sacrifice spread across the country — the songs and poems spoke about the crushing isolation of dark prison cells and the brutalities of the British.

Sometime in the 1970s and 1980s, growing up in the suburbs of a tier-two city in Tamil Nadu, about 50 km from Tirupur, where the 27-year-old Kumaran, famously revered as ‘Kodi Kaatha Kumaran’, chose death over letting the flag fall, and near Coimbatore, where freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaram Pillai was imprisoned, our connect to the freedom struggle was through stories narrated by elders and the patriotic songs aired on Akashvani and Vividh Bharati.

There would be a smattering of Tamil songs, and a few Hindi favourites — ‘Achamillai achamillai acham enbadhillaye’ (there is simply no fear), ‘Vande maataram enbom’ (let’s all chant Vande Mataram), ‘Vaazhga nee emmaan’ (may you live long, a song about how Mahatma Gandhi helped raise a country from the depths of despair), ‘Thaneer vitto valarthom sarvesa’ (did we water the plant called independence? No, we raised it with our tears), and the ubiquitous ‘Saare jahaan se accha’ and ‘Nanna munna rahee hoon’ (made popular by Doordarshan)

A love for the Tamil poet Subramania Bharathi was instilled in us from an early age. In ‘Agnikunjondru kanden’, he writes about finding a tiny spark of fire, hiding it in a hollow in the forest and watching the forest burn down. This idea of igniting a spark seemed to be a recurrent theme in the works of poets and writers in pre-Independence India, and it inspired ordinary people to join the movement.

On the other end of the spectrum was Hindi poet Makhanlal Chaturvedi’s 1921 poem ‘Pushp ki Abhilasha’. It was written from the perspective of a flower that desires to be plucked and placed on the path trodden by the brave who fought for the motherland. The verses tugged at the heartstrings.

Decades later, in 1988, the Lok Seva Sanchar Nigam created a song that reinforced the concept of unity in diversity — ‘Mile sur mera tumhara’, with lyrics in 14 languages, for the youth of the time. It was composed by Ashok Patki and arranged by Louis Banks, and featured well-known names from the field of arts such as vocalists M. Balamuralikrishna, Pt. Bhimsen Joshi, Lata Mangeshkar and Kavita Krishnamurthy, besides film stars such as Amitabh Bachchan, Sharmila Tagore and Waheeda Rehman. The very next year came a 13-minute video ‘Desh Raag’, where musicians and dancers celebrated the cultural plurality and shared national identity through an ancient Hindustani raag.

In 1997, as India rang in 50 years of Independence, composer A.R. Rahman and filmmaker Bharat Bala teamed up for a new version of ‘Vande Mataram’. ‘Maa tujhe salaam’, a track from the album, soon became the anthem of youngsters. Pakistani singer Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan’s ‘Gurus of Peace’, from the album, also became popular. Written by Mehboob, Tim Cody and Dinesh Kapoor, the lyrics went thus: “Boundaries have been drawn on land, but don’t raise a wall between hearts.”

Today, in a deeply cynical world, that age of innocence seems like a distant dream. As nostalgic as this all is, one truly wishes we went back to simpler times where we celebrated commonalities instead of highlighting differences. Bharathi would agree. After all, in his song, ‘Thaayin manikodi paareer’, he asks us to celebrate the diversity of a country that is home to people from varied cultural backgrounds and languages, linked by one common flag.

The first dawn of Independence

Padma Subrahmanyam

I was four then and too young to grasp the historical significance of the day. My father, K.G. Subramanian, a Congressman and filmmaker, had hosted a large feast. Our house in Santhome, spread over 36 acres, was teeming with people: freedom fighters, relatives, artistes and friends. We were used to having guests every day, but that gathering remains etched in my memory. Looking back now, I can imagine the emotions that swept across the nation. One memory stands out clearly: my father asking my mother to compose a special song for me. Standing before the guests, I sang, ‘Gandhi thatha solli paadu paapa…’ What remains with me is not so much the song itself as the atmosphere that surrounded it. The house was filled with people from different walks of life, all united by a sense of joy, relief and hope for the future.

T.V. Gopalakrishnan

I do not particularly like being reminded of that day, because, in many ways, I feel we have let ourselves down as a nation. I often wonder how much we have honoured the sacrifices and commitment of those who fought to secure our freedom, and where we are headed today. I say this because the dawn of Independence was ushered in a truly secular spirit. In Tirupunithura, where I lived, songs by Tagore, Bharati, Kumaran Asan and Vallathol echoed through the streets as people across social and economic divides came together, singing and rejoicing as one.

Umayalpuram Sivaraman

I was 12 years old and studying in the third form. I lived with my paternal grandmother on West Main Street in Thanjavur and attended mridangam lessons twice a day at the home of my guru, the renowned mridangam vidwan Thanjavur Vaidyanatha Iyer, on Pandamanickapa Street. That day, the lanes were so crowded that it was nearly impossible to walk through them. I am 90 and don’t think I have ever witnessed such an outpouring of joy. People dressed in white khadi were all over, singing ‘Vande Mataram’ as they marched. As a teenager, I was excited and joined them in song, sharing in the jubilation of a nation celebrating its newfound freedom.

World.title: Independence Day 2026: Where am I from? The complicated meaning of home for Indians abroad
World.content:
